sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第290卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 290
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 290

sentences.zh: 【後周紀一】起重光大淵獻，盡玄黓困敦八月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Zhou Records 1] From Chongguang Dayuanxian through Xuanyi Kundun, the eighth month; one year and a fraction in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Zhou Records 1] From Chongguang Dayuanxian through Xuanyi Kundun, the eighth month—slightly more than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE)

sentences.zh: 春正月，丁卯，漢<ref>後漢</ref>太后下誥，授監國符寶，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, the Later Han empress dowager issued an edict conferring the regent's seals and treasures and investing him as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, the Later Han empress dowager issued an edict conferring the regent's seals and treasures upon Guo Wei and investing him as emperor.

sentences.zh: 監國自皋門入宮，即位於崇元殿，制曰：「朕周室之裔，虢叔之後，國號宜曰周。

translations.literal: The regent entered the palace through the Gaomen Gate and took the throne in the Chongyuan Hall, proclaiming: "I am a descendant of the Zhou house, a scion of Uncle Guo; the state name should be Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei entered the palace through the Gaomen Gate and took the throne in the Chongyuan Hall, proclaiming: "I am a descendant of the Zhou house, a scion of Uncle Guo; the state name should be Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」改元<ref>廣順</ref>，大赦。

translations.literal: " He changed the era name to Guangshun and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era name to Guangshun and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 楊邠、史弘肇、王章等皆贈官，官為斂葬，仍訪其子孫敘用之。

translations.literal: Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, Wang Zhang, and others were all granted posthumous offices; the state provided their funerals and still sought out their descendants to employ them by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, Wang Zhang, and others were all granted posthumous offices; the state provided their funerals and still sought out their descendants to employ them according to rank.

sentences.zh: 凡倉場、庫務掌納官吏，無得收斗餘、稱耗。

translations.literal: All receiving officials at granaries, depots, and treasury offices were forbidden to collect surplus measures or weighing allowances.
translations.idiomatic: All receiving officials at granaries, depots, and treasury offices were forbidden to collect surplus measures or weighing allowances.

sentences.zh: 舊所羨餘物，悉罷之。

translations.literal: All former surplus levies were entirely abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All former surplus levies were abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: 犯竊盜及奸者，並依晉天福元年以前刑名，罪人非反逆，無得誅及親族，籍沒家貲。

translations.literal: Those guilty of theft or adultery were all judged by the penal names in force before the first year of Later Jin's Tianfu era; for crimes other than treason, kin might not be executed with the offender nor household property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Those guilty of theft or adultery were judged by the penal statutes in force before the first year of Later Jin's Tianfu era; for crimes other than treason, kin might not be executed with the offender nor household property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗<ref>後唐莊宗李存勗</ref>、明宗<ref>後唐明宗李亶</ref>、晉高祖<ref>後晉高祖石敬瑭</ref>各置守陵十房，漢高祖陵職員、宮人，時月薦享及守陵戶並如故。

translations.literal: Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong, Emperor Mingzong, and Later Jin's Emperor Gaozu each had ten households assigned to guard their tombs; the staff, palace women, seasonal offerings, and tomb-guard households for Later Han's Emperor Gaozu remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong, Emperor Mingzong, and Later Jin's Emperor Gaozu each had ten households assigned to guard their tombs; the staff, palace women, seasonal offerings, and tomb-guard households for Later Han's Emperor Gaozu remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，唐衰，多盜，不用律文，更定峻法，竊盜贓三匹者死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tang declined, theft was rampant; disregarding the code, harsher laws were enacted—thieves whose booty reached three bolts of cloth were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Tang declined and theft grew rampant, the authorities set aside the code and enacted harsher laws—thieves whose booty reached three bolts of cloth were put to death.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，加至五匹。

translations.literal: In Later Jin's Tianfu era the threshold was raised to five bolts.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Jin's Tianfu era the threshold was raised to five bolts.

sentences.zh: 奸有夫婦人，無問強、和，男女並死。

translations.literal: For adultery involving a married woman, whether by force or consent, both man and woman were executed.
translations.idiomatic: For adultery involving a married woman, whether by force or consent, both man and woman were executed.

sentences.zh: 漢法，竊盜一錢以上皆死。

translations.literal: Under Later Han law, theft of as little as one cash was capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han law, theft of as little as one cash was punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 又罪非反逆，往往族誅、籍沒，故帝即位，首革其弊。

translations.literal: Moreover, for crimes short of treason, clans were often exterminated and property seized; therefore when the emperor took the throne, he first reformed these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for crimes short of treason, entire clans were often exterminated and property seized; therefore when Guo Wei took the throne, he first reformed these abuses.

sentences.zh: 初，楊邠以功臣、國戚為方鎮者多不閒吏事，乃以三司軍將補都押牙、孔目官、內知客，其人自恃敕補，多專橫，節度使不能制，至是悉罷之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Yang Bin saw that many merit-holders and imperial kin serving as military governors were unskilled in administration, he filled the posts of chief adjutant, clerical officer, and inner guest with army officers from the Three Bureaus; relying on their imperial appointment, they were often overbearing and the governors could not control them—now all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Yang Bin saw that many merit-holders and imperial kin serving as military governors were unskilled in administration, he filled the posts of chief adjutant, clerical officer, and inner guest with army officers from the Three Bureaus; relying on their imperial appointment, they were often overbearing and the governors could not control them—now all were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝命史弘肇親吏上黨李崇矩訪弘肇親族，崇矩言：「弘肇弟弘福今存。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shi Hongzhao's intimate clerk Li Chongju of Shangdang to inquire into Hongzhao's kin; Chongju said: "Hongzhao's younger brother Hongfu is still alive."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Shi Hongzhao's intimate clerk Li Chongju of Shangdang to inquire into Hongzhao's kin; Chongju said: "Hongzhao's younger brother Hongfu is still alive."

sentences.zh: 」初，弘肇使崇矩掌其家貲之籍，由是盡得其產，皆以授弘福。

translations.literal: " Earlier Hongzhao had had Chongju keep the register of his household property; thereby the full estate was obtained and all was given to Hongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hongzhao had had Chongju keep the register of his household property; thereby the full estate was obtained and all was given to Hongfu.

sentences.zh: 帝賢之，使隸皇子榮帳下。

translations.literal: The emperor admired this and had him serve under the prince Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired this and had Hongfu serve under the prince Chai Rong.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以前復州防禦使王彥超權武寧節度使。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the former defender of Fuzhou Wang Yanchao was made acting military governor of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the former defender of Fuzhou Wang Yanchao was made acting military governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 漢李太后遷居西宮，己巳，上尊號曰昭聖皇太后。

translations.literal: The Later Han empress dowager Li moved to the Western Palace; on jisi she was given the honorific title Zhaosheng Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han empress dowager Li moved to the Western Palace; on jisi she was given the honorific title Zhaosheng Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 開封尹兼中書令劉勳卒。

translations.literal: Liu Xun, prefect of Kaifeng and concurrent chief councilor, died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun, prefect of Kaifeng and concurrent chief councilor, died.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，加王峻同平章事。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Wang Jun was made concurrent chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Wang Jun was made concurrent chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 以衛尉卿劉皞主漢隱帝之喪。

translations.literal: The minister of the guards Liu Hao was put in charge of the funeral for Later Han's Emperor Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of the guards Liu Hao was put in charge of the funeral for Later Han's Emperor Yin.

sentences.zh: 初，河東節度使兼中書令劉崇聞隱帝遇害，欲舉兵南向，聞迎立湘陰公，乃止，曰：「吾兒為帝，吾又何求！

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Chong, military governor of Hedong and concurrent chief councilor, hearing that Emperor Yin had been killed, wished to raise troops and march south; hearing that the Duke of Xiangyin had been welcomed to the throne, he stopped and said: "My son is emperor—what more do I want!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Chong, military governor of Hedong and concurrent chief councilor, hearing that Emperor Yin had been killed, wished to raise troops and march south; hearing that Liu Zan, Duke of Xiangyin, had been welcomed to the throne, he stopped and said: "My son is emperor—what more do I want!"

sentences.zh: 」太原少尹李驤陰說崇曰：「觀郭公之心，終欲自取，公不如疾引兵逾太行，據孟津，俟徐州相公即位，然後還鎮，則郭公不敢動矣。

translations.literal: " The Taiyuan vice prefect Li Xiang secretly urged Chong: "Judging Lord Guo's heart, he ultimately intends to seize the throne himself; you had better swiftly lead troops over the Taihang, hold Mengjin, wait until the lord of Xuzhou takes the throne, and then return to your commandery—then Lord Guo will not dare move."
translations.idiomatic: " The Taiyuan vice prefect Li Xiang secretly urged Chong: "Judging Guo Wei's intentions, he ultimately means to seize the throne himself; you had better swiftly lead troops over the Taihang, hold Mengjin, wait until Liu Zan takes the throne at Xuzhou, and then return to your commandery—then Guo Wei will not dare move."

sentences.zh: 不然，且為所賣。

translations.literal: Otherwise you will yet be sold out by him.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you will yet be betrayed by him.

sentences.zh: 」崇怒曰：「腐儒，欲離間吾父子！

translations.literal: " Chong raged: "Rotten pedant—you wish to drive a wedge between father and son!"
translations.idiomatic: " Chong raged: "Rotten pedant—you wish to drive a wedge between father and son!"

sentences.zh: 」命左右曳出斬之。

translations.literal: " He ordered attendants to drag him out and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered attendants to drag him out and behead him.

sentences.zh: 驤呼曰：「吾負經濟之才而為愚人謀事，死固甘心！

translations.literal: Xiang cried out: "I possessed talent for statecraft yet counseled a fool—death I gladly accept!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang cried out: "I possessed talent for statecraft yet counseled a fool—death I gladly accept!"

sentences.zh: 家有老妻，願與之同死。

translations.literal: I have an aged wife at home; I wish to die with her.
translations.idiomatic: I have an aged wife at home; I wish to die with her.

sentences.zh: 」崇並其妻殺之，且奏於朝廷，示無二心。

translations.literal: " Chong killed his wife as well and moreover reported to the court to show he had no divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Chong killed his wife as well and reported to the court to show he had no divided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及贇廢，崇乃遣使請贇歸晉陽。

translations.literal: When Zan was deposed, Chong then sent envoys asking that Zan be returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zan was deposed, Chong then sent envoys asking that Zan be returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 詔報以「湘陰公比在宋州，今方取歸京師，必令得所，公勿以為憂。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "The Duke of Xiangyin is now at Songzhou; he is being brought back to the capital and will certainly be provided for—do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "The Duke of Xiangyin is now at Songzhou; he is being brought back to the capital and will certainly be provided for—do not worry."

sentences.zh: 公能同力相輔，當加王爵，永鎮河東。

translations.literal: If you can lend your strength in support, you will be granted a princely title and hold Hedong in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: If you can lend your strength in support, you will be granted a princely title and hold Hedong in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 」鞏廷美、楊溫聞湘陰公贇失位，奉贇妃董氏據徐州拒守，以俟河東援兵，帝使贇以書諭之。

translations.literal: " Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen, hearing that the Duke of Xiangyin Zan had lost his position, supported Zan's consort Lady Dong in holding Xuzhou and resisting, awaiting Hedong reinforcements; the emperor had Zan write to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: " Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen, hearing that Liu Zan had lost his position, supported Zan's consort Lady Dong in holding Xuzhou and resisting, awaiting Hedong reinforcements; the emperor had Zan write to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 廷美、溫欲降而懼死，帝復遺贇書曰：「爰念斯人盡心於主，足以賞其忠義，何由責以悔尤，俟新節度使入城，當各除刺史，公可更以委曲示之。

translations.literal: Tingmei and Wen wished to surrender but feared death; the emperor again sent Zan a letter saying: "Recalling that these men gave their utmost for their lord, that is enough to reward their loyalty—how can we blame them for regret? When the new military governor enters the city, each shall be made a prefect; you may explain this in detail to them."
translations.idiomatic: Tingmei and Wen wished to surrender but feared death; the emperor again sent Zan a letter saying: "Recalling that these men gave their utmost for their lord, that is enough to reward their loyalty—how can we blame them for regret? When the new military governor enters the city, each shall be made a prefect; you may explain this in detail to them."

sentences.zh: 契丹之攻內丘也，死傷頗多，又值月食，軍中多妖異，契丹主懼，不敢深入，引兵還，遣使請和於漢。

translations.literal: When the Khitan attacked Neiqiu, casualties were heavy; moreover a lunar eclipse occurred and many strange omens appeared in the army—the Khitan ruler was afraid, dared not press deep, withdrew his troops, and sent envoys to seek peace with Han.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan attacked Neiqiu, casualties were heavy; moreover a lunar eclipse occurred and many strange omens appeared in the army—the Khitan ruler was afraid, dared not press deep, withdrew his troops, and sent envoys to seek peace with Later Han.

sentences.zh: 會漢亡，安國節度使劉詞送其使者詣大梁，帝遣左千牛衛將軍朱憲報聘，且敘革命之由，以金器、玉帶贈之。

translations.literal: When Han fell, the Anguo military governor Liu Ci escorted their envoys to Daliang; the emperor sent the Left Imperial Guard general Zhu Xian on a return mission, explaining the cause of the dynastic change, and presented gold vessels and a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Han fell, the Anguo military governor Liu Ci escorted their envoys to Daliang; Guo Wei sent the Left Imperial Guard general Zhu Xian on a return mission, explaining the cause of the dynastic change, and presented gold vessels and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 帝以鄴都鎮撫河北，控制契丹，欲以腹心處之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Yedu pacified Hebei and checked the Khitan, and wished to place a trusted man there.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei considered that Yedu pacified Hebei and checked the Khitan, and wished to place a trusted man there.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以寧江節度使、侍衛親軍都指揮使王殷為鄴都留守、天雄節度使、同平章事，領軍如故，仍以侍衛司從赴鎮。

translations.literal: On yihai, Wang Yin, military governor of Ningjiang and commander of the palace guard, was made Yedu garrison commander, Tianxiong military governor, and concurrent chief councilor, retaining command of the army as before, and the palace guard still accompanied him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Wang Yin, military governor of Ningjiang and commander of the palace guard, was made Yedu garrison commander, Tianxiong military governor, and concurrent chief councilor, retaining command of the army as before, and the palace guard still accompanied him to his post.

sentences.zh: 丙子，帝帥百官詣西宮，為漢隱帝舉哀成服，皆如天子禮。

translations.literal: On bingzi the emperor led the officials to the Western Palace to mourn and don mourning garb for Later Han's Emperor Yin, all according to the rites for an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Guo Wei led the officials to the Western Palace to mourn and don mourning garb for Later Han's Emperor Yin, all according to the rites for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超遣使入貢，帝慮其疑懼，賜詔慰安之，曰：「今兄事已至此，言不欲繁，望弟扶持，同安億兆。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao sent envoys with tribute; the emperor, fearing his suspicion and alarm, bestowed an edict to reassure him, saying: "Now that matters have come to this between elder and younger brother, I do not wish many words—may you, younger brother, lend your support so that we may together secure the myriad people."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao sent envoys with tribute; Guo Wei, fearing his suspicion and alarm, bestowed an edict to reassure him, saying: "Now that matters have come to this between elder and younger brother, I do not wish many words—may you, younger brother, lend your support so that we may together secure the myriad people."

sentences.zh: 戊寅，殺湘陰公於宋州。

translations.literal: On wuyin the Duke of Xiangyin was killed at Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Liu Zan, Duke of Xiangyin, was killed at Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，劉崇即皇帝位於晉陽，仍用乾祐年號，所有者并、汾、忻、代、嵐、憲、隆、蔚、沁、遼、麟、石十二州之地。

translations.literal: That same day Liu Chong took the imperial throne at Jinyang, still using the Qianyou era name; he held the twelve prefectures of Bing, Fen, Xin, Dai, Lan, Xian, Long, Yu, Qin, Liao, Lin, and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Liu Chong took the imperial throne at Jinyang, still using the Qianyou era name; he held the twelve prefectures of Bing, Fen, Xin, Dai, Lan, Xian, Long, Yu, Qin, Liao, Lin, and Shi.

sentences.zh: 以節度判官鄭珙為中書侍郎，觀察判官滎陽趙華為戶部侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: The military governor's aide Zheng Gui was made vice director of the Secretariat, and the surveillance commissioner Zhaoyang Zhao Hua was made vice minister of revenue—both concurrent chief councilors.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor's aide Zheng Gui was made vice director of the Secretariat, and the surveillance commissioner Zhao Hua of Xingyang was made vice minister of revenue—both concurrent chief councilors.

sentences.zh: 以次子承鈞為侍衛親軍都指揮使、太原尹，以節度副使李存瑰為代州防禦使，裨將武安張元徽為馬步軍都指揮使，陳光裕為宣徽使。

translations.literal: His second son Chengjun was made commander of the palace guard and prefect of Taiyuan; the vice military governor Li Cungui was made defender of Daizhou; the staff officer Zhang Yuanhui of Wu'an was made commander of horse and foot; Chen Guangyu was made commissioner of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Liu Chengjun was made commander of the palace guard and prefect of Taiyuan; the vice military governor Li Cungui was made defender of Daizhou; the staff officer Zhang Yuanhui of Wu'an was made commander of horse and foot; Chen Guangyu was made commissioner of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 北漢主謂李存瑰、張元徽曰：「朕以高祖之業，一朝墜地，今日位號，不得已而稱之。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler said to Li Cungui and Zhang Yuanhui: "I have seen Gaozu's enterprise fall to earth in a single morning; today's title I assume only because I must."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong said to Li Cungui and Zhang Yuanhui: "I have seen Gaozu's enterprise fall to earth in a single morning; today's title I assume only because I must."

sentences.zh: 顧我是何天子，汝曹是何節度使邪！

translations.literal: Consider what sort of Son of Heaven I am, and what sort of military governors you are!
translations.idiomatic: Consider what sort of Son of Heaven I am, and what sort of military governors you are!

sentences.zh: 」由是不建宗廟，祭祀如家人，宰相俸錢月止百緡，節度使止三十緡，自餘薄有資給而已，故其國中少廉吏。

translations.literal: " Therefore he did not build an ancestral temple; sacrifices were like those of a household; chief councilors' monthly salary was only a hundred strings, military governors only thirty, and the rest had meager allowances—hence there were few honest officials in his state.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he did not build an ancestral temple; sacrifices were like those of a household; chief councilors' monthly salary was only a hundred strings, military governors only thirty, and the rest had meager allowances—hence there were few honest officials in his state.

sentences.zh: 客省使河南李光美嘗為直省官，頗諳故事，北漢朝廷制度，皆出於光美。

translations.literal: The guest-reception commissioner Li Guangmei of Henan had once been a direct palace clerk and was well versed in precedent; Northern Han court institutions all issued from Guangmei.
translations.idiomatic: The guest-reception commissioner Li Guangmei of Henan had once been a direct palace clerk and was well versed in precedent; Northern Han court institutions all issued from Guangmei.

sentences.zh: 北漢主聞湘陰公死，哭曰：「吾不用忠臣之言，以至於此！

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler, hearing that the Duke of Xiangyin was dead, wept and said: "I did not heed a loyal minister's counsel, and so came to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong, hearing that Liu Zan was dead, wept and said: "I did not heed a loyal minister's counsel, and so came to this!"

sentences.zh: 」為李驤立祠，歲時祭之。

translations.literal: " He erected a shrine for Li Xiang and sacrificed to him at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: He erected a shrine for Li Xiang and sacrificed to him at the seasons.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以太師馮道為中書令，加竇貞固侍中，蘇禹珪司空。

translations.literal: On jimao the grand preceptor Feng Dao was made director of the Secretariat; Dou Zhengu was made palace attendant and Su Yugui minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the grand preceptor Feng Dao was made director of the Secretariat; Dou Zhengu was made palace attendant and Su Yugui minister of works.

sentences.zh: 王彥超奏遣使繼敕詣徐州，鞏廷美等猶豫不肯啟關，詔進兵攻之。

translations.literal: Wang Yanchao memorialized sending envoys with successive edicts to Xuzhou; Gong Tingmei and others hesitated and would not open the gates—an edict ordered troops advanced to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao memorialized sending envoys with successive edicts to Xuzhou; Gong Tingmei and others hesitated and would not open the gates—an edict ordered troops advanced to attack.

sentences.zh: 帝謂王峻曰：「朕起於寒微，備嘗艱苦，遭時喪亂，一旦為帝王，豈敢厚自奉養以病下民乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wang Jun: "I rose from humble origins and have tasted every hardship; encountering an age of turmoil, I became emperor in a day—how would I dare enrich myself at the expense of the people below!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said to Wang Jun: "I rose from humble origins and have tasted every hardship; encountering an age of turmoil, I became emperor in a day—how would I dare enrich myself at the expense of the people below!"

sentences.zh: 」命峻疏四方貢獻珍美食物，庚辰，下詔悉罷之。

translations.literal: " He ordered Jun to list the rare delicacies and fine foods sent as tribute from the four quarters; on gengchen an edict abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jun to list the rare delicacies and fine foods sent as tribute from the four quarters; on gengchen an edict abolished them all.

sentences.zh: 其詔略曰：「所奉止於朕躬，所損被於□庶。

translations.literal: The edict in part said: "What is offered benefits only my person; what is harmed falls upon the common people."
translations.idiomatic: The edict in part said: "What is offered benefits only my person; what is harmed falls upon the common people."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「積於有司之中，甚為無用之物。

translations.literal: " It also said: "Piled up among the offices, they are very much useless things."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "Piled up among the offices, they are very much useless things."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「朕生長軍旅，不親學問，未知治天下之道，文武官有益國利民之術，各具封事以聞，咸宜直書，勿事辭藻。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "I grew up in the army and did not attend to learning; I do not know the way to govern the realm. Civil and military officials who have methods to benefit the state and the people should each submit a sealed memorial, all should write plainly and not deal in ornament."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "I grew up in the army and did not attend to learning; I do not know the way to govern the realm. Civil and military officials who have methods to benefit the state and the people should each submit a sealed memorial, all should write plainly and not deal in ornament."

sentences.zh: 」帝以蘇逢吉之第賜王峻，峻曰：「是逢吉所以族李崧也！

translations.literal: " The emperor gave Wang Jun Su Fengji's mansion; Jun said: "This is the house by which Fengji exterminated Li Song!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei gave Wang Jun Su Fengji's mansion; Jun said: "This is the house by which Fengji exterminated Li Song!"

sentences.zh: 」辭而不處。

translations.literal: " He declined and would not occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: He declined and would not occupy it.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主北歸，橫海節度使潘聿撚棄鎮隨之，契丹主以聿撚為西南路招討使。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Khitan ruler returned north, the Henghai military governor Pan Yunian abandoned his commandery and followed him; the Khitan ruler made Yunian southwest-route pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Khitan ruler returned north, the Henghai military governor Pan Yunian abandoned his commandery and followed him; the Khitan ruler made Yunian southwest-route pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及北漢主立，契丹主使聿撚遺劉承鈞書。

translations.literal: When the Northern Han ruler was established, the Khitan ruler had Yunian send a letter to Liu Chengjun.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong was established as ruler of Northern Han, the Khitan ruler had Yunian send a letter to Liu Chengjun.

sentences.zh: 北漢主使承鈞復書，稱：「本朝淪亡，紹襲帝位，欲循晉室故事，求援北朝。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler had Chengjun reply, stating: "Our dynasty has perished; I have succeeded to the imperial throne and wish to follow the Jin house precedent in seeking aid from the northern court."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong had Chengjun reply, stating: "Our dynasty has perished; I have succeeded to the imperial throne and wish to follow the Jin house precedent in seeking aid from the northern court."

sentences.zh: 」契丹主大喜。

translations.literal: " The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 北漢主發兵屯陰地、黃澤、團柏。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler sent troops to garrison Yindi, Huangze, and Tuanbai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong sent troops to garrison Yindi, Huangze, and Tuanbai.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以承鈞為招討使，與副招討使白從暉、都監李存瑰將步騎萬人寇晉州。

translations.literal: On dinghai Chengjun was made pacification commissioner; with vice commissioner Bai Conghui and overseer Li Cungui he led ten thousand foot and horse to raid Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Liu Chengjun was made pacification commissioner; with vice commissioner Bai Conghui and overseer Li Cungui he led ten thousand foot and horse to raid Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 從暉，吐谷渾人也。

translations.literal: Conghui was a man of the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui was a man of the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 郭崇威更名崇，曹威更名英。

translations.literal: Guo Chongwei changed his name to Chong; Cao Wei changed his name to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongwei changed his name to Chong; Cao Wei changed his name to Ying.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE)

sentences.zh: 春二月丁酉，以皇子天雄牙內都指揮使榮為鎮寧節度使，選朝士為之僚佐，以侍御史王敏為節度判官，右補闕崔頌為觀察判官，校書郎王樸為掌書記。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on dingyou, the prince Rong, inner commander of the Tianxiong guard, was made military governor of Zhenning; court scholars were chosen as his staff—the investigating censor Wang Min as military aide, the right remonstrator Cui Song as surveillance aide, and the proofreader Wang Pu as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on dingyou, Prince Chai Rong, inner commander of the Tianxiong guard, was made military governor of Zhenning; court scholars were chosen as his staff—the investigating censor Wang Min as military aide, the right remonstrator Cui Song as surveillance aide, and the proofreader Wang Pu as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 頌，協之子；

translations.literal: Song was the son of Xie;
translations.idiomatic: Song was the son of Cui Xie;

sentences.zh: 樸，東平人也。

translations.literal: Pu was a man of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was a man of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，北漢兵五道攻晉州，節度使王晏閉城不出。

translations.literal: On wuxu Northern Han troops attacked Jinzhou in five columns; the military governor Wang Yan shut the city and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Northern Han troops attacked Jinzhou in five columns; the military governor Wang Yan shut the city and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 劉承鈞以為怯，蟻附登城。

translations.literal: Liu Chengjun thought him cowardly and swarmed up the walls like ants.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengjun thought him cowardly and swarmed up the walls like ants.

sentences.zh: 晏伏兵奮擊，北漢兵死傷者千餘人。

translations.literal: Yan with ambush troops struck fiercely; Northern Han dead and wounded exceeded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yan with ambush troops struck fiercely; Northern Han dead and wounded exceeded a thousand.

sentences.zh: 承鈞遣副兵馬使安元寶焚晉州西城，元寶來降。

translations.literal: Chengjun sent the vice horse commander An Yuanbao to burn the western quarter of Jinzhou; Yuanbao came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun sent the vice horse commander An Yuanbao to burn the western quarter of Jinzhou; Yuanbao came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 承鈞乃移軍攻隰州。

translations.literal: Chengjun then shifted his army to attack Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun then shifted his army to attack Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，隰州刺史許遷遣步軍都指揮使耿繼業迎擊北漢兵於長壽村，執其將程筠等，殺之。

translations.literal: On guimao the Xizhou prefect Xu Qian sent the foot commander Geng Jiye to meet and strike Northern Han troops at Changshou village; he captured their generals Cheng Yun and others and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Xizhou prefect Xu Qian sent the foot commander Geng Jiye to meet and strike Northern Han troops at Changshou village; he captured their generals Cheng Yun and others and killed them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，北漢兵攻州城，數日不克，死傷甚眾，乃引去。

translations.literal: Before long Northern Han troops attacked the prefectural city; for several days they could not take it, casualties were very heavy, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Northern Han troops attacked the prefectural city; for several days they could not take it, casualties were very heavy, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷，鄆州人也。

translations.literal: Qian was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was a man of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，楚王希萼遣掌書記劉光輔入貢於唐。

translations.literal: On jiachen the Chu king Xi'e sent his chief secretary Liu Guangfu to present tribute to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Chu king Ma Xi'e sent his chief secretary Liu Guangfu to present tribute to Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 帝悉出漢宮中寶玉器數十，碎之於庭，曰：「凡為帝王，安用此物！

translations.literal: The emperor brought out several tens of precious jades and vessels from the Han palace and smashed them in the courtyard, saying: "For one who is emperor, what use are such things!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei brought out several tens of precious jades and vessels from the Han palace and smashed them in the courtyard, saying: "For one who is emperor, what use are such things!"

sentences.zh: 聞漢隱帝日與嬖寵於禁中嬉戲，珍玩不離側，茲事不遠，宜以為鑒！

translations.literal: I hear that Later Han's Emperor Yin daily sported with favorites in the inner palace, curios never leaving his side—this is not far off; take it as a warning!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Later Han's Emperor Yin daily sported with favorites in the inner palace, curios never leaving his side—this is not far off; take it as a warning!"

sentences.zh: 」仍戒左右，自今珍華悅目之物，無得入宮。

translations.literal: " He also admonished those about him: from now on no rare and pleasing objects may enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also admonished those about him: from now on no rare and pleasing objects may enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 丁未，契丹主遣其臣裊骨支與朱憲偕來，賀即位。

translations.literal: On dingwei the Khitan ruler sent his minister Liaoguzhi to come together with Zhu Xian to congratulate him on taking the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the Khitan ruler sent his minister Liaoguzhi to come together with Zhu Xian to congratulate Guo Wei on taking the throne.

sentences.zh: 戊申，敕前資官各聽自便居外州。

translations.literal: On wushen an edict allowed former officials to live where they pleased in outer prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen an edict allowed former officials to live where they pleased in outer prefectures.

sentences.zh: 陳思讓未至湖南，馬希萼已克長沙。

translations.literal: Chen Sirang had not yet reached Hunan when Ma Xi'e had already taken Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sirang had not yet reached Hunan when Ma Xi'e had already taken Changsha.

sentences.zh: 思讓留屯郢州，敕召令還。

translations.literal: Sirang remained garrisoned at Yingzhou; an edict summoned him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Sirang remained garrisoned at Yingzhou; an edict summoned him to return.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，遣尚書左丞田敏使契丹。

translations.literal: On dingsi the Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Tian Min was sent as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Tian Min was sent as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 北漢主遣通事舍人李鞏言使於契丹；

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler sent the communications officer Li Gongyan as envoy to the Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong sent the communications officer Li Gongyan as envoy to the Khitan;

sentences.zh: 乞兵為援。

translations.literal: to beg troops as aid.
translations.idiomatic: to beg troops as aid.

sentences.zh: 詔加泰寧節度使慕容彥超中書令，遣翰林學士魚崇諒詣兗州諭指。

translations.literal: An edict added Murong Yanchao, military governor of Taining, as director of the Secretariat and sent the Hanlin academician Yu Chongliang to Yanzhou to explain the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added Murong Yanchao, military governor of Taining, as director of the Secretariat and sent the Hanlin academician Yu Chongliang to Yanzhou to explain the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 崇諒，即崇遠也。

translations.literal: Chongliang was formerly Chongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongliang was formerly Chongyuan.

sentences.zh: 彥超上表謝。

translations.literal: Yan Chao submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao submitted a memorial expressing his gratitude.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬戌朔，詔報之曰：「向以前朝失德，少主用讒，倉猝之間，召卿赴闕。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the month (the day renxu), an edict replied to him, saying: "Previously, when the former dynasty lost virtue and the young sovereign heeded slander, in sudden haste you were summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day of the month (the day renxu), an imperial reply addressed him: "When the previous regime had forfeited its moral standing and the young emperor was swayed by malicious counsel, you were abruptly summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 卿即奔馳應命，信宿至京，救國難而不顧身，聞君召而不俟駕。

translations.literal: You at once galloped to answer the command; within two nights you reached the capital, saving the state in peril without regard for your own person, hearing the sovereign's call and not waiting for the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: You rode at once to obey the summons and reached the capital within two days. You risked your life to rescue the realm in crisis and came at the ruler's word without waiting for a formal escort.

sentences.zh: 以至天亡漢祚，兵散梁郊，降將敗軍，相繼而至，卿即便回馬首，逕返龜陰。

translations.literal: Thereafter Heaven ended Han's mandate; armies scattered in the Liang suburbs; surrendering generals and defeated troops came in succession; you then turned your horse's head and returned straight to Guiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven withdrew the Han mandate and troops melted away around the Liang capital, you watched defeated commanders and broken armies arrive one after another—then you turned your horse about and rode straight back to Guiyin.

sentences.zh: 為主為時，有終有始。

translations.literal: Toward your lord and toward the times, you had both an end and a beginning.
translations.idiomatic: In your service to your sovereign and to the age, you showed constancy from first to last.

sentences.zh: 所謂危亂見忠臣之節，疾風知勁草之心。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by: in peril and chaos one sees a loyal minister's integrity; in a fierce wind one knows the tough grass's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Truly, danger and disorder reveal a loyal minister's character, and a raging wind tests which grass stands firm.

sentences.zh: 若使為臣者皆能如茲，則有國者誰不欲用！

translations.literal: If all who serve as ministers could be like this, who among those who hold a state would not wish to employ them!
translations.idiomatic: If every subject served with such loyalty, what ruler would not gladly put him to use!

sentences.zh: 所言朕潛龍河朔之際，平難浚郊之時，緣不奉示喻之言，亦不得差人至行闕。

translations.literal: As for what you said—that during my time as a hidden dragon in Heshuo and when I was pacifying crisis at the Jun suburbs—you did not receive our instructions, and therefore could not send men to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: As for your claim that, while I was still in Heshuo before taking the throne and later when I was quelling turmoil near the capital, you received no word from me and so could not dispatch envoys to my camp—

sentences.zh: 且事主之道，何必如斯！

translations.literal: Moreover, in the way of serving one's lord, why must it be so!
translations.idiomatic: surely the duty of a subject need not be carried to such an extreme!

sentences.zh: 若或二三於漢朝，又安肯忠信於周室！

translations.literal: If one were divided two or three ways toward the Han court, how would one be willing to be loyal and faithful to the Zhou house!
translations.idiomatic: A man who wavered between two or three masters under Han would hardly prove steadfast to the Zhou!

sentences.zh: 以此為懼，不亦過乎！

translations.literal: To take this as cause for fear—is it not excessive!
translations.idiomatic: To treat that as grounds for suspicion would be going too far!

sentences.zh: 卿但悉力推心，安民體國，事朕之事，如事故君，不惟黎庶獲安，抑亦社稷是賴。

translations.literal: You need only exhaust your strength with an open heart, settle the people and embody the state, and serve my affairs as you served your former lord's; not only will the common folk obtain peace, but the altars of state will also rely upon you.
translations.idiomatic: Give me your full, open-hearted service: pacify the people, strengthen the realm, and attend to my affairs as faithfully as you once did your former sovereign's. If you do, the common people will find peace and the dynasty itself will rest upon you.

sentences.zh: 但堅表率，未議替移。

translations.literal: Only uphold your role as exemplar; no change or replacement is under discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Hold fast to your post as a model of loyalty; I have no thought of removing or replacing you.

sentences.zh: 由衷之誠，言盡於此。

translations.literal: Sincere feeling from the heart—my words end here.
translations.idiomatic: This is the full measure of my heartfelt intent.

sentences.zh: 唐以楚王希萼為天策上將軍、武安、武平、靜江、寧遠節度使兼中書令、楚王，以右僕射孫晟、客省使姚鳳為冊禮使。

translations.literal: Tang appointed the Prince of Chu, Ma Xie, Heavenly Strategy General-in-Chief, military commissioner of Wu'an, Wuping, Jingjiang, and Ningyuan, concurrently Zhongshu Ling and Prince of Chu; and appointed the Right Vice Director Sun Sheng and the Guest Reception Commissioner Yao Feng as investiture envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Zhou court invested Ma Xie, Prince of Chu, as Heavenly Strategy General-in-Chief and military commissioner of Wu'an, Wuping, Jingjiang, and Ningyuan, with the additional titles of Zhongshu Ling and Prince of Chu. Sun Sheng, the Right Vice Director, and Yao Feng, the Guest Reception Commissioner, were sent as envoys to conduct the investiture.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，遣前淄州刺史陳思讓將兵戍磁州，扼黃澤路。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the former prefect of Zi Prefecture, Chen Siren, was dispatched to lead troops to garrison Ci Prefecture and block the Huangze route.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingyin, Chen Siren, former prefect of Zi Prefecture, was sent with troops to hold Ci Prefecture and seal off the Huangze road.

sentences.zh: 楚王希萼既得志，多思舊怨，殺戮無度，晝夜縱酒荒淫，悉以軍府事委馬希崇。

translations.literal: Once the Prince of Chu, Ma Xie, had achieved his ambition, he brooded over old grudges and killed without measure; day and night he indulged in wine and debauchery, and entrusted all military and prefectural affairs to Ma Xichong.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Xie, Prince of Chu, had secured power, he nursed old grievances and slaughtered without restraint. He spent his days and nights in drunken revelry and handed every matter of command and administration to Ma Xichong.

sentences.zh: 希崇復多私曲，政刑紊亂。

translations.literal: Xichong also had many private partialities, and government and punishments fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong, for his part, played favorites freely, and law and discipline collapsed into confusion.

sentences.zh: 府庫既盡於亂兵，籍民財以賞繼士卒，或封其門而取之，士卒猶以不均怨望。

translations.literal: The treasury had already been emptied by mutinous troops; he registered the people's wealth to reward the remaining soldiers, sometimes sealing their doors to seize it; the soldiers still resented the unequal shares.
translations.idiomatic: Mutineers had already drained the treasury, so he registered civilian property to pay the troops who remained—sometimes sealing a household's doors and taking everything by force. Even so, the soldiers grumbled that the rewards were unfair.

sentences.zh: 雖朗州舊將佐從希萼來者，亦皆不悅，有離心。

translations.literal: Even the old Lingzhou generals and aides who had come with Xie were all displeased and harbored thoughts of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Even the veteran officers from Langzhou who had followed Xie southward were unhappy and began to turn away from him.

sentences.zh: 劉光輔之入貢於唐也，唐主待之厚，光輔密言：「湖南民疲主驕，可取也。

translations.literal: When Liu Guangfu came to pay tribute to Tang, the Tang ruler treated him generously; Guangfu said secretly, "The people of Hunan are weary and the ruler is arrogant—it can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Guangfu arrived at the Later Zhou court to pay tribute, the emperor received him warmly. Guangfu confided, "The people of Hunan are exhausted and their ruler is arrogant. The province can be taken."

sentences.zh: 」唐主乃以營屯都虞候邊鎬為信州刺史，將兵屯袁州，潛圖進取。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler then appointed the Battalion Garrison Chief of Staff Bian Hao as prefect of Xin Prefecture, to lead troops stationed at Yuan Prefecture and secretly plan an advance to seize the region.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor thereupon appointed Bian Hao, chief of staff of the encamped armies, prefect of Xin Prefecture, and ordered him to encamp at Yuan Prefecture with troops while secretly preparing an offensive.

sentences.zh: 小門使謝彥顒，本希萼家奴，以首面有寵於希萼，至與妻妾雜坐，恃恩專橫。

translations.literal: The Small Gate Commissioner Xie Yanyan had originally been a household slave of Xie's; because his face was favored, Xie favored him, even allowing him to sit among wives and concubines; relying on favor, he acted with arbitrary arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: The Small Gate Commissioner Xie Yanyan had begun life as a household slave in Ma Xie's service. His handsome face won Xie's favor to such a degree that he was permitted to sit among the prince's wives and concubines, and he abused that privilege to bully others at will.

sentences.zh: 常肩隨希崇，或拊其背，希崇銜之。

translations.literal: He often walked shoulder to shoulder with Xichong, sometimes patting his back; Xichong bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently walked arm in arm with Xichong and would even clap him on the back. Xichong swallowed his anger.

sentences.zh: 故事，府宴，小門使執兵在門外。

translations.literal: By precedent, at prefectural banquets the Small Gate Commissioner stood armed outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, at headquarters banquets the Small Gate Commissioner stood guard with weapons outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 希萼使彥顒預坐，或居諸將之上，諸將皆恥之。

translations.literal: Xie had Yanyan take a seat in advance, sometimes above the various generals; all the generals were shamed by it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie seated Yanyan among the guests, sometimes above his senior commanders—a humiliation every general felt keenly.

sentences.zh: 希萼以府捨焚蕩，命朗州靜江指揮使王逵、副使周行逢帥所部兵千餘人治之，執役甚勞，又無犒賜，士卒皆怨，竊言曰：「囚免死則役作之。

translations.literal: Because the prefectural quarters had been burned and looted, Xie ordered the Langzhou Jingjiang Commander Wang Kui and the Vice Commissioner Zhou Xingfeng to lead more than a thousand men of their command to repair them; the corvée labor was very arduous and there were no rewards; the soldiers all resented it and whispered, saying, "Prisoners spared from death are put to forced labor.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters buildings were burned and wrecked, Ma Xie ordered Wang Kui, commander of the Jingjiang force at Langzhou, and Vice Commissioner Zhou Xingfeng to bring more than a thousand of their men to rebuild them. The work was brutal and unrewarded, and the men muttered among themselves: "Only condemned men who escape execution are put to hard labor.

sentences.zh: 我輩從大王出萬死取湖南，何罪而囚役之！

translations.literal: We followed the Great King through ten thousand deaths to take Hunan—what crime is this, that we are imprisoned and enslaved!
translations.idiomatic: We followed the Great King through mortal peril to conquer Hunan—what offense have we committed that we should be treated like convicts!"

sentences.zh: 且大王終日酣歌，豈知我輩之勞苦乎！

translations.literal: And the Great King sings drunk all day—does he know our toil and hardship!
translations.idiomatic: The Great King spends his days in drunken song—does he know anything of our suffering?"

sentences.zh: 」逵、行逢聞多，相謂曰：「眾怨深矣，不早為計，禍及吾曹。

translations.literal: Kui and Xingfeng heard much of this and said to each other, "The men's resentment runs deep; if we do not act soon, disaster will reach us."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui and Zhou Xingfeng heard enough of this to alarm them. "The troops' anger has gone too far," they said to each other. "If we do not move quickly, we shall be ruined with them."

sentences.zh: 」壬申旦，帥其眾各執長柯斧、白梃，逃歸朗州。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day renshen, they led their men, each grasping long-handled axes and white clubs, and fled back to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the day renshen they marched their men out of camp, each man carrying a long-handled axe or a white club, and fled back toward Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 時希萼醉未醒，左右不敢白。

translations.literal: At the time Xie was drunk and not yet awake; those around him dared not inform him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie was still drunk and asleep, and none of his attendants dared tell him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，始白之。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, they at last informed him.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the following day, guiyou, did anyone finally report it to him.

sentences.zh: 希萼遣湖南指揮使唐師翥將千餘人追之，不及，直抵朗州。

translations.literal: Xie dispatched the Hunan Commander Tang Shizhu to lead more than a thousand men in pursuit; he could not overtake them and went straight on to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie sent Tang Shizhu, commander of the Hunan force, after them with more than a thousand men. Shizhu failed to catch them and pressed on directly to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 逵等乘其疲乏，伏兵縱擊，士卒死傷殆盡，師翥脫歸。

translations.literal: Kui and the others, taking advantage of their exhaustion, set an ambush and struck; the soldiers were dead and wounded nearly to the last man; Shizhu escaped back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui and his companions, catching the pursuers spent and weary, lay in ambush and attacked. Tang Shizhu's force was nearly annihilated; he alone escaped back.

sentences.zh: 逵等黜留後馬光贊，更以希萼兄子光惠知州事。

translations.literal: Kui and the others deposed the acting governor Ma Guangzan and replaced him with Xie's elder brother's son Guanghui to manage prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and his allies removed the acting governor Ma Guangzan and installed Ma Xie's nephew Ma Guanghui to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 光惠，希振之子也。

translations.literal: Guanghui was the son of Xizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghui was the son of Ma Xizhen.

sentences.zh: 尋奉光惠為節度使，逵等與何敬真及諸軍指揮使張倣參決軍府事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they installed Guanghui as military commissioner; Kui and the others, together with He Jingzhen and the various army commanders including Zhang Fang, jointly decided military and prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they invested Guanghui as military commissioner. Wang Kui, Zhou Xingfeng, He Jingzhen, and the army commanders, among them Zhang Fang, shared authority over military and administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 希萼具以狀言於唐，唐主遣使以厚賞招諭之。

translations.literal: Xie fully reported the circumstances to Tang; the Tang ruler sent envoys with generous rewards to summon and persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie sent a full account of the revolt to the Later Zhou court, and the emperor dispatched envoys bearing rich gifts to win the rebels back with persuasion.

sentences.zh: 逵等納其賞，縱其使，不答其詔，唐亦不敢詰也。

translations.literal: Kui and the others accepted the rewards, released the envoys, and did not reply to the edict; Tang also did not dare to press the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took the gifts, sent the envoys on their way, and ignored the imperial message. The Zhou court, for its part, did not dare press the issue.

sentences.zh: 王彥超奏克徐州，殺鞏廷美等。

translations.literal: Wang Yanchao memorialized that he had captured Xu Prefecture and killed Gong Tingmei and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao reported that he had taken Xu Prefecture and executed Gong Tingmei and his associates.

sentences.zh: 北漢李鞏言至契丹，契丹主使拽剌梅裡報之。

translations.literal: Li Gongyan of Northern Han reached the Khitan; the Khitan ruler sent Zhaila Meili to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongyan's mission from Northern Han reached the Khitan court, and the Khitan emperor sent Zhaila Meili to relay the reply.

sentences.zh: 丙子，敕：「朝廷與唐本無仇怨，緣淮軍鎮，各守疆域，無得縱兵民擅入唐境。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, an edict stated: "The court and Tang originally have no enmity; along the Huai, military garrisons shall each guard their territories and must not allow troops and civilians to enter Tang territory at will.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi an edict declared: "Our court bears no old grudge against Southern Tang. Garrisons along the Huai shall remain within their borders and must not let soldiers or civilians cross into Tang territory at will.

sentences.zh: 商旅往來，無得禁止。

translations.literal: Merchants and travelers coming and going must not be prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and travelers passing back and forth must not be obstructed."

sentences.zh: 己卯，潞州送涉縣所獲北漢將卒二百六十餘人，各賜衫褲巾履遣還。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, Lu Prefecture sent the more than two hundred sixty Northern Han generals and soldiers captured at She County; each was given shirts, trousers, headcloths, and shoes and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, Lu Prefecture forwarded more than two hundred sixty Northern Han officers and men captured in She County. Each was given clothing and footwear and sent home.

sentences.zh: 加吳越王弘俶諸道兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: Wu-Yue King Hongchu was promoted to All-Circuit Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hongchu, King of Wuyue, was elevated to All-Circuit Marshal.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬辰朔，濱淮州鎮上言：「淮南饑民過淮糴谷，未敢禁止。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the first day of the month (the day renchen), the prefectures and garrisons along the Huai reported: "Starving people from Huainan cross the Huai to buy grain; we dare not forbid them."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the first day of the month (the day renchen), authorities along the Huai River reported: "Famine refugees from Huainan are crossing the river to buy grain, and we have not dared to stop them."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「彼之生民，與此何異，宜令州縣津舖無得禁止。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Their living people—how do they differ from ours? Prefectures, counties, ferries, and posts are ordered not to forbid them."
translations.idiomatic: The court replied: "Those people are no different from our own. Let every prefecture, county, ferry, and post allow them to pass without hindrance."

sentences.zh: 蜀通奏使高延昭固辭知樞密院，丁未，以前雲安榷鹽使太原伊審征為通奏使，知樞密院事。

translations.literal: The Shu Communications Commissioner Gao Yanzhao firmly declined to oversee the Palace Secretariat; on the day dingwei, the former Yun'an Salt Monopoly Commissioner Yin Shenzheng of Taiyuan was appointed Communications Commissioner and charged with Palace Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanzhao, the Shu court's communications commissioner, firmly refused to head the Palace Secretariat. On the day dingwei, Yin Shenzheng of Taiyuan, former commissioner of the Yun'an salt monopoly, was made communications commissioner and put in charge of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 審征，蜀高祖妹褒國公主之子也，少與蜀主相親狎，及知樞密，政之大小悉以咨之。

translations.literal: Shenzheng was the son of Shu Gaozu's sister, the Princess of Baoguo; in youth he was intimate with the Shu ruler; once he oversaw the Palace Secretariat, affairs great and small were all referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzheng was the son of the Princess of Baoguo, a sister of the Shu founding emperor. He had been close to the present Shu ruler since youth, and once he took charge of the Palace Secretariat every matter, large or small, passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 審征亦以經濟為己任，而貪侈回邪，與王昭遠相表裡，蜀政由是浸衰。

translations.literal: Shenzheng also took governance as his own task, but he was greedy, extravagant, and crooked; with Wang Zhaoyuan he acted inside and outside in concert, and Shu governance thereby gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzheng styled himself a man of statecraft, yet he was greedy, lavish, and corrupt. Working hand in glove with Wang Zhaoyuan, he helped send Shu governance into steady decline.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘俶徙廢王弘倧居東府，為築宮室，治園圃，娛悅之，歲時供饋甚厚。

translations.literal: Wu-Yue King Hongchu moved the deposed king Hongzong to reside at the Eastern Prefecture, built palace quarters for him, tended gardens, amused him, and supplied him generously at each season.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hongchu, King of Wuyue, resettled the deposed Qian Hongzong in the Eastern Prefecture. He built him a residence, laid out gardens for his pleasure, and sent lavish seasonal gifts.

sentences.zh: 契丹主遣使如北漢，告以周使田敏來，約歲輸錢十萬緡。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler sent an envoy to Northern Han, informing them that the Zhou envoy Tian Min had come and agreeing on an annual tribute of one hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor sent envoys to Northern Han with word that the Later Zhou envoy Tian Min had arrived and that yearly tribute of one hundred thousand strings of cash had been agreed upon.

sentences.zh: 北漢主使鄭珙以厚賂謝契丹，自稱「侄皇帝致書於叔天授皇帝」，請行冊禮。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler sent Zheng Gui with rich gifts to thank the Khitan, styling himself "Nephew Emperor writing to Uncle Heaven-Received Emperor," and requesting the investiture ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong dispatched Zheng Gui with lavish presents to thank the Khitan court, addressing himself as "Nephew Emperor, writing to Uncle Heaven-Received Emperor," and asking that the formal investiture be performed.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)

sentences.zh: 夏五月己巳，遣左金吾將軍姚漢英等使於契丹，契丹留之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, on the day jisi, the Left Jinwu General Yao Hanying and others were dispatched as envoys to the Khitan; the Khitan detained them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the day jisi, Yao Hanying of the Left Jinwu Guard and others were sent as envoys to the Khitan court—and the Khitan detained them.

sentences.zh: 辛未，北漢禮部侍郎、同平章事鄭珙卒於契丹。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, the Northern Han Ministry of Rites Vice Director and Fellow Grand Councilor Zheng Gui died in Khitan territory.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, Zheng Gui, vice director of the Northern Han Ministry of Rites and fellow grand councilor, died while still in Khitan lands.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，義武節度使孫方簡避皇考諱，更名方諫。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, the Yiwu Military Commissioner Sun Fangjian, avoiding the taboo on the imperial father's name, changed his name to Fangjian.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Sun Fangjian, military commissioner of Yiwu, changed his name to Fangjian to avoid the taboo on Guo Wei's father's name.

sentences.zh: 定難節度使李彝殷遣使奉表於北漢。

translations.literal: The Dingnan Military Commissioner Li Yiyin sent an envoy presenting a memorial to Northern Han.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiyin, military commissioner of Dingnan, sent an envoy with a formal memorial to the Northern Han court.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)

sentences.zh: 夏六月辛亥，以樞密使、同平章事王峻為左僕射兼門下侍郎，樞密副使、兵部侍郎范質、戶部侍郎、判三司李穀為中書侍郎，並同平章事，谷仍判三司。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer, on the day xinhai, the Palace Secretariat Commissioner and Fellow Grand Councilor Wang Jun was appointed Left Vice Director and concurrently Gate Down Vice Director; the Palace Secretariat Deputy Commissioner and Ministry of War Vice Director Fan Zhi, and the Ministry of Revenue Vice Director and Overseer of the Three Departments Li Gu were appointed Zhongshu Vice Directors, all as Fellow Grand Councilors; Gu continued to oversee the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer, on the day xinhai, Wang Jun, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and fellow grand councilor, was made Left Vice Director and concurrently Gate Down Vice Director. Fan Zhi, deputy commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and vice director of the Ministry of War, and Li Gu, vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and overseer of the Three Departments, were appointed Zhongshu Vice Directors and fellow grand councilors; Li Gu retained charge of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 司徒兼侍中竇貞固、司空兼中書侍郎、同平章事蘇禹珪並罷守本官。

translations.literal: The Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant Dou Zhengu, and the Grand Preceptor, Zhongshu Vice Director, and Fellow Grand Councilor Su Yugui were both dismissed from their concurrent posts and kept their original offices.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Zhengu, grand mentor and palace attendant, and Su Yugui, grand preceptor, Zhongshu vice director, and fellow grand councilor, were both removed from their chief posts and retained only their base ranks.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，范質參知樞密院事。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Fan Zhi was assigned to participate in overseeing Palace Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou, Fan Zhi was given a role in the management of Palace Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以宣徽北院使翟光鄴兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, the Xuanhui North Court Commissioner Zhai Guangye was additionally appointed Palace Secretariat Deputy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi, Zhai Guangye, commissioner of the Xuanhui North Court, was also made deputy commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，帝討河中，已為人望所屬。

translations.literal: Initially, when the emperor campaigned against Hezhong, he was already the object of popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Even before he took the throne, when Guo Wei marched against Hezhong, the people already looked to him as their hope.

sentences.zh: 李穀時為轉運使，帝數以微言諷之，穀但以人臣盡節為對，帝以是賢之。

translations.literal: Li Gu was at the time transport commissioner; the emperor several times used subtle words to hint at his intentions, but Gu answered only with a subject's full loyalty; the emperor therefore esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu was then transport commissioner. Guo Wei more than once tested him with oblique remarks, but Gu replied only with the language of unwavering service. The emperor came to admire him for it.

sentences.zh: 即位，首用為相。

translations.literal: Upon enthronement, he was first appointed chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei ascended the throne, Li Gu was among the first men elevated to the chief council.

sentences.zh: 時國家新造，四方多故，王峻夙夜盡心，知無不為，軍旅之謀，多所裨益。

translations.literal: At the time the state was newly founded and troubles abounded on all sides; Wang Jun toiled day and night with full heart, leaving nothing undone that he knew how to do; military plans owed much to his contribution.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty was newly established and threats pressed from every quarter. Wang Jun worked day and night without reserve, turning his hand to whatever needed doing, and the army's strategy owed much to his counsel.

sentences.zh: 范質明敏強記，謹守法度。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi was bright, nimble, and strong in memory, and carefully observed laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi was quick-witted and possessed a formidable memory; he upheld the law with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 李穀沉毅有器略，在帝前議論，辭氣慷慨，善譬諭以開主意。

translations.literal: Li Gu was deep, steady, and possessed capacity and strategy; before the emperor in discussion his words were fervent in spirit, and he was good at using analogies to open the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu was grave, resolute, and far-sighted. In council before Guo Wei he spoke with passionate clarity and had a gift for framing arguments that opened the ruler's mind.

sentences.zh: 武平節度使馬光惠，愚懦嗜酒，不能服諸將，王逵、周行逢、何敬真謀以辰州刺史廬陵劉言驍勇得蠻夷心，欲迎以為副使。

translations.literal: The Wuping Military Commissioner Ma Guanghui was foolish, cowardly, and fond of wine, and could not command the various generals; Wang Kui, Zhou Xingfeng, and He Jingzhen plotted that because the Chen Prefecture prefect Liu Yan of Luling was valiant and brave and had won the hearts of the barbarian tribes, they wished to welcome him as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guanghui, military commissioner of Wuping, was dull, timid, and addicted to wine, and he could not keep the generals in line. Wang Kui, Zhou Xingfeng, and He Jingzhen decided that Liu Yan of Luling, prefect of Chen Prefecture—a fierce fighter trusted by the tribal peoples—should be brought in as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 言知逵等難制，曰：「不往，將攻我。

translations.literal: Yan knew that Kui and the others would be hard to control and said, "If I do not go, they will attack me."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan knew the others would be difficult to manage. "If I refuse to go," he said, "they will turn on me."

sentences.zh: 」乃單騎赴之。
既至，眾廢光惠，送於唐，推言權武平留後，表求旄節於唐，唐人未許。

translations.literal: He then went alone on horseback to them; once he arrived, the crowd deposed Guanghui, sent him to Tang, and pushed Yan to act as acting Wuping governor; they memorialized requesting banner and axe from Tang, but the Tang court did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out alone to meet them. Once he arrived, the mutineers deposed Guanghui, sent him to the Later Zhou court, and installed Liu Yan as acting governor of Wuping. They petitioned Zhou for formal commission, but the court withheld its approval.

sentences.zh: 亦稱籓於周。

translations.literal: They also declared themselves vassals of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: They nevertheless acknowledged Zhou suzerainty.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘俶以前內外馬步都統軍使仁俊無罪，復其官爵。

translations.literal: Wu-Yue King Hongchu, because the former Inner and Outer Horse and Infantry Commander Renjun was innocent, restored his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hongchu, King of Wuyue, restored the titles and office of Ren Jun, former commander of the inner and outer horse and infantry forces, declaring that he had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣燕王述軋等冊命北漢王為大漢神武皇帝，妃為皇后。

translations.literal: The Khitan dispatched the Prince of Yan, Shuzha, and others to invest the Northern Han ruler as Great Han Divine Martial Emperor and his consort as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent the Prince of Yan, Shuzha, and a party of envoys to invest Liu Chong as Emperor Divine and Martial of Great Han and to elevate his consort as empress.

sentences.zh: 北漢主更名旻。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler changed his name to Min.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong took the personal name Min.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)

sentences.zh: 秋七月，北漢主遣翰林學士博興衛融等詣契丹謝冊禮，且請兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, the Northern Han ruler dispatched the Hanlin Academician Wei Rong of Boxing and others to go to the Khitan to thank them for the investiture and also to request troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Liu Chong sent Wei Rong of Boxing, a Hanlin academician, and others to the Khitan court to give thanks for the investiture and to ask for military aid.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)

sentences.zh: 秋八月，壬戌，葬漢隱帝於穎陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on the day renxu, the Han Hidden Emperor was buried at Ying Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on the day renxu, the late Han emperor Yin was interred at Ying Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 義武節度使孫方諫入朝，壬子，徙鎮國節度使，以其弟易州刺史行友為義武留後。

translations.literal: The Yiwu Military Commissioner Sun Fangjian entered court; on the day renzi he was transferred to Zhenguo Military Commissioner, and his younger brother, the Yi Prefecture prefect Xingyou, was made acting Yiwu governor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fangjian, military commissioner of Yiwu, came to court. On the day renzi he was reassigned to Zhenguo, and his younger brother Xingyou, prefect of Yi Prefecture, was left behind as acting governor of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 又徙建雄節度使於晏鎮徐州，以武寧節度使王彥超代之。

translations.literal: The Jianxiong Military Commissioner was also transferred—Yan moved to Xu Prefecture—and the Wuning Military Commissioner Wang Yanchao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The post of Jianxiong military commissioner was likewise rotated: Yan was moved to Xu Prefecture, and Wang Yanchao, military commissioner of Wuning, took his place.

sentences.zh: 戊午，追立故夫人柴氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, the late Lady Chai was posthumously established as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu, the late Lady Chai was posthumously enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE.)

sentences.zh: 秋九月，北漢主遣招討使李存瑰將兵自團柏入寇。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn, the Northern Han ruler dispatched the Pacification Commissioner Li Cunkui to lead troops invading from Tuanbai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, Liu Chong sent Pacification Commissioner Li Cunkui with an army to raid southward from Tuanbai.

sentences.zh: 契丹欲引兵會之，與酋長議於九十九泉。

translations.literal: The Khitan wished to lead troops to join him and discussed with the chieftains at Ninety-Nine Springs.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor intended to march south in support and convened the tribal chiefs for counsel at Ninety-Nine Springs.

sentences.zh: 諸部皆不欲南寇，契丹主強之。

translations.literal: All the tribes were unwilling to raid southward; the Khitan ruler forced them.
translations.idiomatic: Every tribe resisted a southern campaign, but the Khitan emperor overruled them and pressed on.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，行至新州之西火神澱，燕王述軋及偉王之子太寧王漚僧作亂，弒契丹主而立述軋。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, when they had reached west of Xin Prefecture at Fire God Shoals, the Prince of Yan Shuzha and the Great King's son, the Prince of Taiping Huseng, rebelled, assassinated the Khitan ruler, and enthroned Shuzha.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai, as the army reached Fire God Shoals west of Xin Prefecture, the Prince of Yan, Shuzha, and Huseng, Prince of Taiping and son of the Great King, rose in revolt, killed the Khitan emperor, and proclaimed Shuzha ruler in his place.

sentences.zh: 契丹主德光之子齊王述律逃入南山，諸部奉述律以攻述軋、漚僧，殺之，並其族黨。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler Deguang's son, the Prince of Qi Shulü, fled into the Southern Mountains; the various tribes rallied to Shulü to attack Shuzha and Huseng, killed them, and exterminated their clans and partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang's son, Prince of Qi Shulü, took refuge in the Southern Mountains. The tribal divisions rallied behind him, struck down Shuzha and Huseng, and wiped out their kin and followers.

sentences.zh: 立述律為帝，改元應歷。

translations.literal: They established Shulü as emperor and changed the era name to Yingli.
translations.idiomatic: Shulü was enthroned as emperor, and the reign era was renamed Yingli.

sentences.zh: 自火神澱入幽州，遣使告於北漢，北漢主遣樞密直學士上黨王得中如契丹，賀即位，復以叔父事之，請兵以擊晉州。

translations.literal: From Fire God Shoals he entered You Prefecture, dispatched envoys to inform Northern Han; the Northern Han ruler sent Privy Direct Academician Wang Dezong of Shangdang to the Khitan court to congratulate him on his accession, again treated him as an uncle, and requested troops to attack Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After marching from Fire God Shoals into You Prefecture, the new Khitan emperor sent word to Northern Han. Liu Chong dispatched Privy Direct Academician Wang Dezong of Shangdang to congratulate him on taking the throne, renewed the custom of addressing him as uncle, and asked for Khitan troops to strike Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 契丹主年少，好遊戲，不親國事，每夜酣飲，達旦乃寐，日中方起，國人謂之睡王。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was young, fond of games, and did not personally attend to state affairs; each night he drank heavily until dawn before sleeping, and only rose at midday—the people called him the Sleeping King.
translations.idiomatic: The young Khitan emperor cared only for sport and left government unattended. He caroused every night until dawn, slept through the morning, and did not rise until noon, so his subjects nicknamed him the Sleeping King.

sentences.zh: 後更名明。

translations.literal: Later he was renamed Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He later changed his name to Ming.

sentences.zh: 壬申，蜀以吏部尚書、御史中丞范仁恕為中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Shu appointed Minister of Civil Appointments and Censor-in-Chief Fan Renshu as Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Minister of Civil Appointments and Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Later Shu named Fan Renshu—Minister of Civil Appointments and Censor-in-Chief—Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Civil Appointments, and Chief Councillor.

sentences.zh: 楚王希萼既克長沙，不賞許可瓊，疑可瓊怨望，出為蒙州刺史。

translations.literal: King of Chu Ma Xie'e, having conquered Changsha, did not reward Xu Keqiong; suspecting that Keqiong harbored resentment, he sent him out as Prefect of Meng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Xie'e seized Changsha, he gave Xu Keqiong no reward for his service. Fearing resentment, he banished Keqiong to the post of prefect of Meng.

sentences.zh: 遣馬步都指揮使徐威、左右軍馬步使陳敬遷、水軍都指揮使魯公館、牙內侍衛指揮使陸孟俊帥部兵立寨於城西北隅，以備朗兵。

translations.literal: He dispatched Infantry and Cavalry Commander-in-Chief Xu Wei, Left-Right Army Infantry-Cavalry Commander Chen Jingqian, Naval Commander-in-Chief Lu Gongguan, and Palace Guard Commander Lu Mengjun to lead their units and establish camps at the northwest corner of the city to guard against troops from Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Infantry and Cavalry Commander Xu Wei, Left-Right Army Commander Chen Jingqian, Naval Commander Lu Gongguan, and Palace Guard Commander Lu Mengjun with their detachments in camps outside the northwest wall to hold Langzhou at bay.

sentences.zh: 不存撫役者，將卒皆怨怒，謀作亂。

translations.literal: He did not care for or comfort those serving in corvée; officers and soldiers were all resentful and angry, and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Because he showed no concern for the men laboring on his works, officers and rank-and-file alike seethed with anger and began plotting mutiny.

sentences.zh: 希崇知其謀，戊寅，希萼宴將吏，徐威等不預，希崇亦辭疾不至。

translations.literal: Ma Xiechong learned of the plot; on the day wuyin, Ma Xie'e held a banquet for officers, but Xu Wei and the others were not invited, and Xiechong also declined on grounds of illness and did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiechong got wind of the conspiracy. On wuyin, Ma Xie'e hosted a feast for his commanders, but Xu Wei and his confederates were left off the guest list, and Xiechong pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 威等使人先驅踶嚙馬十餘入府，自帥其徒執斧斤、白梃，聲言縶馬，奄至座上，縱橫擊人，顛踣滿地。

translations.literal: Wei and the others had men first drive more than ten kicking and biting horses into the mansion; they themselves led their followers wielding axes and white clubs, claiming they were restraining the horses, suddenly arrived at the banquet seats, struck people wildly, and people fell overturned all over the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wei first sent a dozen unruly horses stampeding into the hall, then rushed in at the head of his men with axes and white staves, shouting that they were corralling the beasts. They fell upon the banquet in a frenzy, beating guests until the floor was strewn with bodies.

sentences.zh: 希萼逾垣走，威等執囚之。

translations.literal: Ma Xie'e climbed over the wall and fled; Wei and the others seized and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie'e scrambled over the wall and escaped, but Wei and his men captured him and threw him in chains.

sentences.zh: 執謝彥顒，自頂及踵剉之。

translations.literal: They seized Xie Yanyong and shaved him from crown to heel.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Xie Yanyong and shaved him bald from head to foot.

sentences.zh: 立希崇為武安留後，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: They enthroned Ma Xiechong as acting military governor of Wu'an and let the troops plunder extensively.
translations.idiomatic: They installed Ma Xiechong as acting military governor of Wu'an and turned the soldiers loose on a general sack of the city.

sentences.zh: 幽希萼於衡山縣。

translations.literal: They confined Ma Xie'e in Hengshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie'e was imprisoned in Hengshan County.

sentences.zh: 劉言聞希崇立，遣兵趣潭州，聲言討其篡奪之罪。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, hearing that Ma Xiechong had been installed, dispatched troops toward Tan Prefecture, proclaiming that he would punish the crime of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan learned that Ma Xiechong had seized power, he marched on Tan Prefecture under the banner of punishing usurpation.

sentences.zh: 壬午，軍於益陽之西。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, the army encamped west of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu his army halted west of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 希崇懼，癸未，發兵二千拒之，又遣使如朗州求和，請為鄰籓。

translations.literal: Ma Xiechong was afraid; on the day guiwei, he sent two thousand troops to resist, and also dispatched envoys to Lang Prefecture seeking peace, requesting to be neighboring vassals.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Ma Xiechong on guiwei sent two thousand men to block Liu Yan's advance and dispatched envoys to Langzhou offering peace and asking to remain a neighboring vassal state.

sentences.zh: 掌書記桂林李觀象說言曰：「希萼舊將佐猶在長沙，此必不欲與公為鄰；

translations.literal: Secretariat aide Li Guanxiang of Guilin advised Liu Yan, saying: "Ma Xie'e's former officers and aides still remain in Changsha— they surely do not wish to be your neighbor;
translations.idiomatic: Li Guanxiang of Guilin, Liu Yan's secretariat aide, urged him: "Ma Xie'e's old commanders and staff are still in Changsha. They will never accept you as a neighbor—

sentences.zh: 不若先檄希崇取其首，然後圖湖南，可兼有也。

translations.literal: it would be better first to issue an edict to Ma Xiechong demanding their heads, then afterward plan for Hunan—you can take it all."
translations.idiomatic: Better to order Xiechong to deliver their heads first, then move on Hunan. That way you can take the whole province."

sentences.zh: 」言從之。

translations.literal: Liu Yan followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 希崇畏言，即斷都軍判官楊仲敏、掌書記劉光輔、牙內指揮使魏師進、都押牙黃勍等十餘人首，遣前辰陽縣令李翊繼送朗州。

translations.literal: Ma Xiechong, fearing Liu Yan, immediately beheaded more than ten men including Army adjutant Yang Zhongmin, secretariat aide Liu Guangfu, inner guard commander Wei Shijin, and chief military adjutant Huang Qin, and sent former Chenyang county magistrate Li Yi to deliver the heads to Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cowed by Liu Yan, Xiechong at once executed more than ten men—among them Army adjutant Yang Zhongmin, secretariat aide Liu Guangfu, inner guard commander Wei Shijin, and chief adjutant Huang Qin—and sent former Chenyang magistrate Li Yi to Langzhou with their heads.

sentences.zh: 至則腐敗，言與王逵等皆以為非仲敏等首，怒責翊，翊惶恐自殺。

translations.literal: When they arrived the heads were already decayed; Liu Yan and Wang Kui and the others all believed they were not the heads of Zhongmin and the rest, angrily rebuked Li Yi, and Yi in terror killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the heads reached Langzhou they had rotted beyond recognition. Liu Yan, Wang Kui, and the rest were convinced they were not Yang Zhongmin's party at all. They raged at Li Yi, who in panic took his own life.

sentences.zh: 希崇既襲位，亦縱酒荒淫，為政不公，語多矯妄，國人不附。

translations.literal: Ma Xiechong, having usurped the throne, also indulged in wine and debauchery, governed unfairly, his words were mostly pretentious and extravagant, and the people of the state did not support him.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, Ma Xiechong sank into drunken excess, ruled unjustly, and filled his mouth with grandiose boasts. The people of Chu would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 初，馬希萼入長沙，彭師暠雖免死，猶杖背黜為民。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ma Xie'e entered Changsha, Peng Shigao, though spared death, was still beaten on the back and demoted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Xie'e first took Changsha, Peng Shigao had been spared execution but was flogged and stripped of rank, reduced to a commoner.

sentences.zh: 希崇以為師暠必怨之，使送希萼於衡山，實欲師暠殺之。

translations.literal: Ma Xiechong thought Peng Shigao must resent him and had Ma Xie'e escorted to Hengshan, actually intending for Shigao to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiechong assumed Shigao bore a grudge and had Xie'e sent to Hengshan, hoping Shigao would murder him.

sentences.zh: 師暠曰：「欲使我為弒君之人乎！

translations.literal: Peng Shigao said: "Do you wish to make me a regicide!"
translations.idiomatic: Shigao replied: "Do you mean to make me a king-slayer?"

sentences.zh: 」奉事逾謹。

translations.literal: He served Ma Xie'e with even greater diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he waited on Xie'e with redoubled care.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，至衡山。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, they reached Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu they arrived at Hengshan.
