sentences.zh: 衡山指揮使廖偃，匡圖之子也，與其季父節度巡官匡凝謀曰：「吾家世受馬氏恩，今希萼長而被黜，必不免禍，盍相與輔之！

translations.literal: Hengshan commander Liao Yan, son of Kuang Tu, and his younger uncle, circuit patrol officer Kuang Ning, plotted together, saying: "Our family has received the Ma clan's kindness for generations; now Ma Xie'e is the elder yet was deposed—he is sure to meet disaster—why not jointly assist him!"
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yan, Hengshan's commander and son of Kuang Tu, and his uncle Kuang Ning, a circuit patrol officer, agreed: "Our house has owed the Ma clan a debt of gratitude for generations. Xie'e is the elder brother yet was cast out—disaster will surely find him. Let us rally to his side!"

sentences.zh: 」於是帥莊戶及鄉人悉為兵，與帥暠共立希萼為衡山王，以縣為行府，斷江為柵，編竹為戰艦，以師暠為武清節度使，召募徒眾，數日，至萬餘人，州縣多應之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they led estate households and villagers all as soldiers, and together with Peng Shigao enthroned Ma Xie'e as King of Hengshan, made the county their mobile headquarters, cut the river with palisades, wove bamboo into war boats, appointed Peng Shigao military commissioner of Wuqing, recruited followers—within days they reached over ten thousand, and many prefectures and counties responded.
translations.idiomatic: They mobilized every estate tenant and villager they could muster, and with Shigao proclaimed Xie'e King of Hengshan. The county became their field headquarters: they blocked the river with a palisade, lashed bamboo into warships, and made Shigao military commissioner of Wuqing. Within days their ranks swelled past ten thousand, and prefectures and counties across the region began to answer their call.

sentences.zh: 遣判官劉虛己求援於唐。

translations.literal: They dispatched adjutant Liu Xuji to request aid from Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Liu Xuji was sent to Southern Tang to plead for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 徐威等見希崇所為，知必無成，又畏朗州、衡山之逼，恐一朝喪敗，俱及禍，欲殺希崇以自解。

translations.literal: Xu Wei and the others, seeing Ma Xiechong's conduct, knew he would certainly fail, and fearing the pressure from Lang Prefecture and Hengshan, afraid that if they failed in a moment all would suffer calamity, wished to kill Ma Xiechong to extricate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Watching Xiechong's misrule, Xu Wei and his faction saw that he was doomed. With Langzhou and Hengshan pressing in, they feared a sudden collapse that would drag them all down, and resolved to kill Xiechong to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 希崇微覺之，大懼，密遣客將范守牧奉表請兵於唐，唐主命邊鎬自袁州將兵萬人西趣長沙。

translations.literal: Ma Xiechong faintly sensed this, was greatly afraid, secretly dispatched guest officer Fan Shoumu to submit a memorial requesting troops from Southern Tang; the Southern Tang ruler ordered Bian Hao to lead ten thousand men from Yuan Prefecture westward toward Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Xiechong had a dim sense of the plot and was terrified. He secretly sent guest officer Fan Shoumu to Southern Tang with a plea for troops. The Southern Tang emperor ordered Bian Hao to march ten thousand men west from Yuanzhou toward Changsha.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元九五一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 951 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, the year 951 CE)

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛卯，潞州巡檢陳思讓敗北漢兵於虒亭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day xinmao, Luzhou inspector Chen Sirang defeated Northern Han troops at Si Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on xinmao, Chen Sirang, inspector of Luzhou, routed a Northern Han force at Si Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 唐邊鎬引兵入醴陵。

translations.literal: Southern Tang's Bian Hao led troops into Liling.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao of Southern Tang advanced into Liling.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，楚王希崇遣使犒軍。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, King of Chu Ma Xiechong dispatched envoys to reward the army with provisions.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, King Ma Xiechong sent envoys to bring supplies and cheer Bian Hao's army.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，遣天策府學士拓跋恆奉箋詣鎬請降。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, he dispatched Tian Ce Fu academician Tuoba Heng bearing a letter to Bian Hao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he sent Tian Ce Fu academician Tuoba Heng with a written submission offering surrender to Bian Hao.

sentences.zh: 恆歎曰：「吾久不死，乃為小兒送降狀！

translations.literal: Tuoba Heng sighed, saying: "I have long not died, only to hand in a surrender petition for this boy!"
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Heng sighed: "I clung to life all these years only to deliver a surrender note for this whelp!"

sentences.zh: 」癸卯，希崇帥弟侄迎鎬，望塵而拜，鎬下馬稱詔勞之。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Ma Xiechong led younger brothers and nephews to greet Bian Hao, bowing as they saw the dust of his approach; Bian Hao dismounted and read an imperial message to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Xiechong went out with younger brothers and nephews to meet Bian Hao, prostrating themselves in the dust of his column. Bian Hao dismounted and, in the emperor's name, offered words of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，希崇等從鎬入城，鎬捨於瀏陽門樓，湖南將吏畢賀，鎬皆厚賜之。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Ma Xiechong and the others followed Bian Hao into the city; Bian Hao lodged at Liuyang Gate tower, all Hunan officers and officials came to congratulate, and Bian Hao generously rewarded them all.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Xiechong and his party entered the city with Bian Hao, who took up quarters in the Liuyang Gate tower. Every Hunan officer and official came to pay homage, and Bian Hao lavished gifts on them all.

sentences.zh: 時湖南饑饉，鎬大發馬氏倉粟賑之，楚人大悅。

translations.literal: At that time Hunan was suffering famine; Bian Hao greatly opened the Ma clan's granaries to relief them, and the people of Chu were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was in the grip of famine. Bian Hao threw open the Ma family's storehouses and distributed grain on a vast scale, and the people of Chu rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣彰國節度使蕭禹厥將奚、契丹五萬會北漢兵入寇。

translations.literal: The Khitan dispatched Zhangguo military commissioner Xiao Yujue leading fifty thousand Xi and Khitan troops to join Northern Han forces in invading.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Zhangguo military commissioner Xiao Yujue at the head of fifty thousand Xi and Khitan warriors to link up with Northern Han for a joint invasion.

sentences.zh: 北漢主自將兵二萬自陰地關寇晉州，丁未，軍於城北，三面置寨，晝夜攻之，遊兵至絳州。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler personally led twenty thousand troops from Yindi Pass to raid Jin Prefecture; on the day dingwei, the army camped north of the city, established camps on three sides, attacked day and night, and raiding parties reached Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong himself led twenty thousand men through Yindi Pass against Jinzhou. On dingwei his army encircled the north side of the city, threw up camps on three faces, and hammered the walls day and night while raiders pushed as far as Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時王晏已離鎮，王彥超未至，巡檢使王萬敢權知晉州，與龍捷都指揮使史彥超、虎捷指揮使何徽共拒之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yan had left his post and Wang Yanchao had not yet arrived; inspector Wang Wan'gan was acting governor of Jin Prefecture, and together with Dragon Swift commander Shi Yanchao and Tiger Swift commander He Hui jointly resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan had already departed his command and Wang Yanchao had not yet arrived, so inspector Wang Wan'gan held Jinzhou in an acting capacity. He stood with Dragon Swift commander Shi Yanchao and Tiger Swift commander He Hui to meet the assault.

sentences.zh: 史彥超，雲州人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yanchao was a native of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanchao came from Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，唐武昌節度使劉仁贍帥戰艦二百取岳州，撫納降附，人忘其亡。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Southern Tang Wuchang military commissioner Liu Renshan led two hundred warships to take Yue Prefecture, comforting and accepting surrendering adherents—people forgot their state's fall.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Liu Renshan, Southern Tang's military commissioner of Wuchang, seized Yuezhou with two hundred warships. He treated the surrendered population so gently that people scarcely remembered their kingdom was lost.

sentences.zh: 仁贍，金之子也。

translations.literal: Liu Renshan was the son of Liu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan was a son of Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 唐百官共賀湖南平，起居郎高遠曰：「我乘楚亂，取之甚易。

translations.literal: Southern Tang officials together congratulated the pacification of Hunan; Court Diarist Gao Yuan said: "We took advantage of Chu's disorder—seizing it was very easy."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang court celebrated the conquest of Hunan. Court Diarist Gao Yuan remarked: "We moved while Chu was tearing itself apart—taking the province was the easy part."

sentences.zh: 觀諸將之才，但恐守之難耳！

translations.literal: "Looking at the generals' talents, I only fear holding it will be difficult!"
translations.idiomatic: "Judging by the caliber of our commanders, I suspect keeping it will prove the hard part!"

sentences.zh: 」遠，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Gao Yuan was a native of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuan was from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 司徒致仕李建勳曰：「禍其始此乎！

translations.literal: Retired Grand Preceptor Li Jianxun said: "Does disaster begin from this!"
translations.idiomatic: Retired Grand Preceptor Li Jianxun murmured: "Is this where the trouble starts?"

sentences.zh: 」唐主自即位以來，未嘗親祠郊廟，禮官以為請。

translations.literal: Since the Southern Tang ruler's accession, he had never personally performed suburban and temple rites; ritual officials requested it.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he took the throne, the Southern Tang emperor had never personally offered at the suburban altars or ancestral temples, and the masters of ceremony had repeatedly pressed him to do so.

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「俟天下一家，然後告謝。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler said: "Wait until the realm is one family, then I will report and give thanks."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "I shall wait until the realm is united under one house, and only then report my thanks to Heaven and the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」及一舉取楚，謂諸國指麾可定。

translations.literal: And with one stroke taking Chu, he believed the various states could be directed and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Chu had fallen in a single campaign, he assumed the remaining kingdoms could be brought to heel at a gesture.

sentences.zh: 魏岑侍宴言：「臣少游元城，樂其風土，俟陛下定中原，乞魏博節度使。

translations.literal: At a banquet Wei Cen attended, he said: "In my youth I traveled to Yuancheng and enjoyed its customs; when Your Majesty settles the Central Plains, I beg to be military commissioner of Weibo."
translations.idiomatic: At court Wei Cen, attending a banquet, said: "I once traveled to Yuancheng as a young man and loved the country there. When Your Majesty pacifies the Central Plains, I ask only to be made military commissioner of Weibo."

sentences.zh: 」唐主許之，岑趨下拜謝。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler agreed; Wei Cen hurried down to bow in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented, and Cen scurried from his seat to kowtow in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 其主驕臣佞如此。

translations.literal: Thus arrogant was the ruler and fawning the minister.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the arrogance of the sovereign and the sycophancy of his courtier.

sentences.zh: 馬希萼望唐人立己為潭帥，而潭人惡希萼，共請邊鎬為帥，唐主乃以鎬為武安節度使。

translations.literal: Ma Xie'e hoped the Tang people would install him as Tan prefect, but the people of Tan hated Ma Xie'e and together requested Bian Hao as commander, so the Southern Tang ruler made Bian Hao military commissioner of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie'e had expected the Southern Tang to name him prefect of Tan, but the people of Tan despised him and petitioned collectively for Bian Hao. The Southern Tang emperor therefore appointed Bian Hao military commissioner of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 王峻有故人曰申師厚，嘗為兗州牙將，失職饑寒，望峻馬拜謁於道。

translations.literal: Wang Jun had an old acquaintance named Shen Shihou who had once been a Yan Prefecture guard officer; having lost his position he suffered hunger and cold, and seeing Wang Jun's horse he bowed in greeting on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's old friend Shen Shihou had once served as a guard officer at Yanzhou. Out of office, hungry and ragged, he spotted Wang Jun on the road and bowed deeply from beside the horse.

sentences.zh: 會涼州留後折逋嘉施上表請帥於朝廷，帝以絕域非人所欲，募率府供奉官願行者，月餘，無人應募，峻薦師厚於帝。

translations.literal: At this time the Liangzhou acting governor Zhebo Jiashi submitted a memorial requesting a commander from court; the emperor considered that this remote region was not what people desired, and solicited Palace Attendant officials willing to go—for over a month none volunteered, and Wang Jun recommended Shihou to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the acting governor of Liangzhou, Zhebo Jiashi, petitioned the throne for a new commander. The emperor knew the far frontier was no man's wish, and called for Palace Attendants willing to take the post. For more than a month no one stepped forward, and Wang Jun put Shihou's name before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以師厚為河西節度使。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, Shen Shihou was appointed military commissioner of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Shen Shihou was named military commissioner of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 唐邊鎬趣馬希崇帥其族入朝，馬氏聚族相泣，欲重賂鎬，奏乞留居長沙。

translations.literal: Southern Tang's Bian Hao urged Ma Xiechong to lead his clan to court; the Ma clan gathered and wept together, wishing to bribe Bian Hao heavily and petitioned to remain living in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao pressed Ma Xiechong to bring the whole clan to the Southern Tang capital. The Ma family gathered in tears, hoping to buy him off with a heavy bribe and begging permission to stay in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 鎬微曬曰：「國家與公家世為仇敵，殆六十年，然未嘗敢有意窺公之國。

translations.literal: Bian Hao smiled slightly, saying: "Our state and your family have been mortal enemies for nearly sixty years, yet we never dared harbor intent to covet your state."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao gave a thin smile. "Our two houses have been enemies for nearly sixty years, yet we never once dared set our sights on your kingdom."

sentences.zh: 今公兄弟斗鬩，困窮自歸，若復二三，恐有不測之憂。

translations.literal: "Now your brothers quarrel, and in distress you come of your own accord—if this happens again a second or third time, I fear there may be unforeseeable troubles."
translations.idiomatic: "Your brothers turned on each other, and you came to us in desperation. If such chaos repeats itself once or twice more, I cannot answer for what may follow."

sentences.zh: 」希崇無以應，十一月，辛酉，與宗族及將佐千餘人號慟登舟，送者皆哭，響振川谷。

translations.literal: Ma Xiechong had nothing to reply; in the eleventh month, on the day xinyou, together with over a thousand clansmen and officers he wailed and boarded ship; all who saw them off wept, the sound echoing through valleys and streams.
translations.idiomatic: Xiechong had no reply. In the eleventh month, on xinyou, he boarded ship with more than a thousand kinsmen and officers, wailing as they departed. Those left on the shore wept until the sound rolled through the hills and watercourses.

sentences.zh: 帝以北漢、契丹之兵猶在晉州，甲子，以王峻為行營都部署，將兵救之。

translations.literal: Because Northern Han and Khitan troops were still at Jin Prefecture, on the day jiazi the emperor appointed Wang Jun as overall commander of the mobile camp and led troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: With Northern Han and Khitan forces still pressing Jinzhou, the Later Zhou emperor on jiazi named Wang Jun overall commander of the relief expedition and sent him west with an army.

sentences.zh: 詔諸軍皆受峻節度，聽以便宜從事，得自選擇將吏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all armies to obey Wang Jun's command, permitting him to act as expedient, and to select officers himself.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict placed every unit under Wang Jun's authority, authorized him to act at discretion, and allowed him to appoint his own officers.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，峻行，帝自至城西餞之。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Wang Jun departed; the emperor personally went to the west of the city to farewell feast him.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Wang Jun marched out, and the emperor himself rode west of the capital to see him off with a farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 楚靜江節度副使、知桂州馬希隱，武穆王殷之少子也。

translations.literal: Chu's Jingjiang deputy military commissioner and acting Guilin prefect Ma Xiyin was the youngest son of Prince Wumu Ma Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiyin, deputy military commissioner of Jingjiang and acting prefect of Guilin, was the youngest son of Prince Wumu Ma Yin.

sentences.zh: 楚王希廣、希萼兄弟爭國，南漢主以內侍使吳懷恩為西北招討使，將兵屯境上，伺間密謀進取。

translations.literal: When the brothers Kings Ma Xiguang and Ma Xie'e of Chu contended for the realm, the Southern Han ruler appointed inner palace envoy Wu Huai'en as Northwest Pacification Commissioner, stationing troops on the border and watching for an opportunity to advance.
translations.idiomatic: While Ma Xiguang and Ma Xie'e fought over Chu, the Southern Han emperor made inner palace envoy Wu Huai'en Northwest Pacification Commissioner, massing troops on the frontier and waiting for a chance to strike.

sentences.zh: 希廣遣指揮使彭彥暉將兵屯龍峒以備之。

translations.literal: Ma Xiguang dispatched commander Peng Yanhui to garrison Longdong to guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiguang posted commander Peng Yanhui at Longdong to block them.

sentences.zh: 希萼自衡山遣使以彥暉為桂州都監、在城外內巡檢使、判軍府事，希隱惡之，潛遣人告蒙州刺史許可瓊。

translations.literal: Ma Xie'e from Hengshan sent envoys appointing Peng Yanhui as Guilin director, inner and outer patrol commissioner outside the walls, and military prefecture judge; Ma Xiyin resented this and secretly sent word to Meng Prefecture prefect Xu Keqiong.
translations.idiomatic: From Hengshan, Ma Xie'e sent orders naming Yanhui Guilin's director, commissioner for patrol inside and outside the walls, and judge of the military prefecture. Xiyin bristled at the appointment and secretly alerted Xu Keqiong, prefect of Meng.

sentences.zh: 可瓊方畏南漢之逼，即棄蒙州，引兵趣桂州，與彥暉戰於城中。

translations.literal: Xu Keqiong was then afraid of Southern Han pressure, immediately abandoned Meng Prefecture, led troops toward Guilin, and fought Peng Yanhui within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiong, already fearing Southern Han, at once abandoned Mengzhou, marched on Guilin, and clashed with Yanhui inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 彥暉敗，奔衡山，可瓊留屯桂州。

translations.literal: Peng Yanhui was defeated, fled to Hengshan; Xu Keqiong remained garrisoned at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was beaten and fled to Hengshan. Keqiong stayed to hold Guilin.

sentences.zh: 吳懷恩據蒙州，進兵侵掠，桂管大擾，希隱、可瓊不知所為，但相與飲酒對泣。

translations.literal: Wu Huai'en seized Meng Prefecture, advanced troops to raid and plunder—Guilin circuit was greatly disturbed; Ma Xiyin and Xu Keqiong knew not what to do, only drank wine together and wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Huai'en took Mengzhou and pushed forward in a wave of raids that threw Guilin circuit into turmoil. Xiyin and Keqiong were at their wits' end and could do nothing but sit together over wine, weeping face to face.

sentences.zh: 南漢主遺希隱書，言：「武穆王奄有全楚，富強安靖五十餘年。

translations.literal: The Southern Han ruler sent Ma Xiyin a letter, saying: "Prince Wumu held all of Chu—prosperous, strong, and tranquil for more than fifty years."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Han emperor wrote to Xiyin: "Prince Wumu once held all of Chu in prosperity and peace for more than fifty years."

sentences.zh: 正由三十五舅、三十舅兄弟尋戈，自相魚肉，舉先人基業，北面仇讎。

translations.literal: "Precisely because the Thirty-Fifth Uncle and Thirty-Sixth Uncle, the brothers, took up spears against each other, devoured one another's flesh, and turned the ancestors' foundation over to the northern enemy."
translations.idiomatic: "Then the Thirty-Fifth and Thirty-Sixth Uncles turned on each other with blades, tore the realm apart, and handed your forefathers' legacy to a northern foe."

sentences.zh: 今聞唐兵已據長沙，竊計桂林繼為所取。

translations.literal: "Now I hear Tang troops have already occupied Changsha—I reckon Guilin will next be taken."
translations.idiomatic: "Now I learn that Southern Tang holds Changsha, and I expect Guilin will fall next."

sentences.zh: 當朝世為與國，重以婚姻，睹茲傾危，忍不赴救！

translations.literal: "Our court has for generations been allied states, bound further by marriage—seeing this crisis, how could we bear not to rush to rescue!"
translations.idiomatic: "Our courts have been allies for generations, tied moreover by marriage. Seeing you in peril, how could we stand by?"

sentences.zh: 已發大軍水陸俱進，當令相公舅永擁節旄，常居方面。

translations.literal: "I have already dispatched a great army advancing by land and water—you shall forever hold the command banner and remain in your region."
translations.idiomatic: "I have already sent a great host by land and river. You shall keep your command and hold your post in perpetuity."

sentences.zh: 」希隱得書，與僚佐議降之，支使潘玄珪以為不可。

translations.literal: Ma Xiyin, receiving the letter, consulted with aides about surrendering; administrative aide Pan Xuangui held it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the letter reached Xiyin, he discussed surrender with his staff. Administrative aide Pan Xuangui argued against it.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，吳懷恩引兵奄至城下，希隱、可瓊帥其眾，夜斬關奔全州，桂州遂潰。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Wu Huai'en led troops suddenly to the city walls; Ma Xiyin and Xu Keqiong led their masses, by night cut through the gate and fled to Quan Prefecture—Guilin immediately collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Wu Huai'en appeared suddenly beneath the walls. Xiyin and Keqiong led their men out by night, broke through the gate, and fled to Quanzhou. Guilin fell at once.

sentences.zh: 懷恩因以兵略定宜、連、梧、嚴、富、昭、柳、象、龔等州，南漢始盡有嶺南之地。

translations.literal: Wu Huai'en then with troops subdued Yi, Lian, Wu, Yan, Fu, Zhao, Liu, Xiang, Gong and other prefectures—Southern Han for the first time fully possessed the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en went on to overrun Yi, Lian, Wu, Yan, Fu, Zhao, Liu, Xiang, Gong, and the rest. For the first time Southern Han held all of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 辛未，唐邊鎬遣先鋒指揮使李承戩將兵如衡山，趣馬希萼入朝。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Southern Tang's Bian Hao dispatched vanguard commander Li Chengkan leading troops to Hengshan, urging Ma Xie'e to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Bian Hao sent vanguard commander Li Chengkan to Hengshan to escort Ma Xie'e to the Southern Tang court.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，希萼與將佐士卒萬餘人自潭州東下。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Ma Xie'e together with officers and soldiers numbering over ten thousand descended eastward from Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Xie'e set out east from Tanzhou with more than ten thousand officers and men.

sentences.zh: 王峻留陝州旬日，帝以北漢攻晉州急，憂其不守，議自將由澤州路與峻會兵救之，且遣使諭峻。

translations.literal: Wang Jun stayed at Shan Prefecture ten days; the emperor, because Northern Han's attack on Jin Prefecture was urgent, worried it would not hold, discussed personally leading troops by the Ze Prefecture route to join Wang Jun's forces for relief, and also dispatched envoys to inform Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun halted at Shanzhou for ten days. The emperor, alarmed that Jinzhou might fall under the fierce Northern Han assault, debated leading an army himself by way of Zezhou to join Wang Jun and sent messengers ahead to tell him so.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊子朔，下詔以三日西征。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day wuzi, an edict was issued to westward campaign on the third day.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month, wuzi, an edict announced that the emperor would march west in three days.

sentences.zh: 使者至陝，峻因使者言於帝曰：「晉州城堅，未易可拔，劉崇兵鋒方銳，不可力爭。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Shan, Wang Jun through the envoy told the emperor: "Jin Prefecture's walls are strong, not easily taken; Liu Chong's troops' edge is now sharp, one cannot fight by force."
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger reached Shanzhou, Wang Jun sent back word: "Jinzhou's walls are stout and will not yield quickly. Liu Chong's men are at the peak of their fighting spirit—we should not meet them head-on."

sentences.zh: 所以駐兵，待其氣衰耳，非臣怯也。

translations.literal: "The reason I station troops is to wait until their morale declines—it is not that your servant is cowardly."
translations.idiomatic: "I am holding my position only until their ardor fades. This is not cowardice on my part."

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位，不宜輕動。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty has newly acceded—you should not move lightly."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty has only just taken the throne. You ought not stir yourself rashly."

sentences.zh: 若年駕出汜水，則慕容彥超引兵入汴，大事去矣！

translations.literal: "If the imperial carriage goes beyond Sishui, Murong Yanchao will lead troops into Bian—the great matter will be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: "If you cross Sishui in person, Murong Yanchao will march on Bianliang and everything we have built will be undone!"

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，自以手提耳曰：「幾敗吾事！

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing this, himself grabbing his ear said: "I nearly ruined my enterprise!"
translations.idiomatic: When the message reached him, the emperor clutched his own ear and exclaimed: "I almost wrecked everything!"

sentences.zh: 」庚寅，敕罷親征。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, an edict halted the personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin an edict canceled the emperor's planned personal expedition.

sentences.zh: 初，泰寧節度使兼中書令慕容彥超聞徐州平，疑懼愈甚，乃招納亡命，畜聚薪糧，潛以書結北漢，吏獲其書以聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Taining military commissioner and concurrent Palace Director Murong Yanchao, hearing Xuzhou pacified, suspicion and fear grew ever greater; he recruited fugitives, stored firewood and grain, secretly sent letters to ally with Northern Han, and officials seized the letters and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Murong Yanchao, military commissioner of Taining and concurrent Palace Director, had grown ever more fearful after hearing that Xuzhou was pacified. He gathered desperadoes, stockpiled fuel and grain, and secretly opened correspondence with Northern Han until officials intercepted the letters and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又遣人詐為商人求援於唐。

translations.literal: He also sent men posing as merchants to seek aid from Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched agents disguised as traders to solicit help from Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 帝遣通事舍人鄭好謙就申慰諭，與之為誓。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Protocol Gentleman Zheng Haoqian to go explain and comfort, and made oaths with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Protocol Gentleman Zheng Haoqian to reassure him in person and exchanged sworn pledges with him.

sentences.zh: 彥超益不自安，屢遣都押牙鄭麟詣闕，偽輸誠款，實覘機事。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao grew ever more uneasy, repeatedly sent chief adjutant Zheng Lin to court, falsely offering sincerity, actually to reconnoiter opportunities.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao only grew more restless. Again and again he sent chief adjutant Zheng Lin to the capital with professions of loyalty, while in truth probing for a chance to move.

sentences.zh: 又獻天平節度使高行周書，其言皆謗毀朝廷與彥超相結之意。

translations.literal: He also submitted a letter from Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Tianping; its words all expressed the intent of slandering the court and colluding with Yanchao.
translations.idiomatic: He also turned in a letter purportedly from Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Tianping, full of accusations that the court was in league with Yanchao.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「此彥超之詐也！

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "This is Yanchao's fraud!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "This is Yanchao's trickery!"

sentences.zh: 」以書示行周，行周上表謝恩。

translations.literal: He showed the letter to Xingzhou; Xingzhou submitted a memorial thanking the grace.
translations.idiomatic: He showed the letter to Xingzhou, who submitted a memorial of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 既而彥超反跡益露，丙申，遣閣門使張凝將兵赴鄆州巡檢以備之。

translations.literal: Before long Yanchao's rebellious signs grew ever clearer; on bingshen the emperor dispatched Gate Attendant Zhang Ning to lead troops to Yan Prefecture for inspection as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yanchao's rebellion showed itself more plainly. On bingshen the emperor sent Gate Attendant Zhang Ning with troops to Yan Prefecture on an inspection tour to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 庚子，王峻至絳州。

translations.literal: On gengzi Wang Jun reached Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Wang Jun reached Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乙已，引兵趣晉州。

translations.literal: On yisi he led troops toward Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he marched toward Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晉州南有蒙坑，最為險要，峻憂北漢兵據之。

translations.literal: South of Jin Prefecture was Meng Pit, the most perilous strongpoint; Jun feared Northern Han troops would seize it.
translations.idiomatic: South of Jin Prefecture lay Meng Pit, the most dangerous pass on the route, and Jun feared the Northern Han would hold it.

sentences.zh: 是日，聞前鋒已度蒙坑，喜曰：「吾事濟矣！

translations.literal: That day, hearing the vanguard had already crossed Meng Pit, he rejoiced and said: "My task is accomplished!"
translations.idiomatic: That day, when he learned the vanguard had already crossed Meng Pit, he exclaimed in delight, "The day is won!"

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超奏請入朝，帝知其詐，即許之。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao memorialized requesting to come to court; the emperor knew it was a ruse and at once granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao asked permission to come to court. The emperor saw through the pretense and granted it at once.

sentences.zh: 既而復稱境內多盜，未敢離鎮。

translations.literal: Before long he again claimed that bandits were rife within his circuit and that he dared not leave his post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he pleaded again that bandits were rampant in his circuit and that he dared not leave his post.

sentences.zh: 北漢主攻晉州，久不克。

translations.literal: Northern Han forces pressed the attack on Jin Prefecture but for a long time could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Han forces pressed the siege of Jin Prefecture but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，民相聚保山寨，野無所掠，軍乏食。

translations.literal: Just then heavy snow fell; the people gathered in mountain strongholds for protection, there was nothing to plunder in the countryside, and the army lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell. The people took refuge in mountain stockades, the countryside offered nothing to plunder, and the army ran short of provisions.

sentences.zh: 契丹思歸，聞王峻至蒙坑，燒營夜遁。

translations.literal: The Khitan longed to return home; hearing Wang Jun had reached Meng Pit, they burned their camps and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were eager to go home. When they heard Wang Jun had reached Meng Pit, they burned their camps and slipped away in the night.

sentences.zh: 峻入晉州，諸將請亟追之，峻猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Jun entered Jin Prefecture; the generals asked to pursue at once, but Jun hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Jun entered Jin Prefecture. The generals urged an immediate pursuit, but he wavered and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 明日，乃遣行營馬軍都指揮使仇弘超、都排陳使藥元福、左廂排除使陳思讓、康延沼將騎兵追之，及於霍邑，縱兵奮擊，北漢兵墜崖谷死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The next day he dispatched Field Army Cavalry Commander Qiu Hongchao, Chief Formation Officer Yao Yuanfu, Left Wing Exclusion Officer Chen Sirang, and Kang Yanzhao to lead cavalry in pursuit; at Huoyi they unleashed their troops in fierce attack, and very many Northern Han soldiers fell to their deaths in cliffs and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent Field Army Cavalry Commander Qiu Hongchao, Chief Formation Officer Yao Yuanfu, Left Wing Exclusion Officer Chen Sirang, and Kang Yanzhao in pursuit with the cavalry. At Huoyi they charged hard, and Northern Han soldiers tumbled by the hundreds into the gorges below.

sentences.zh: 霍邑道隘，延沼畏懦不急追，由是北漢兵得度。

translations.literal: The road at Huoyi was narrow; Yanzhao was timid and did not press the pursuit, and so Northern Han troops were able to get across.
translations.idiomatic: The road through Huoyi was narrow. Yanzhao lost his nerve and failed to press the chase, and the Northern Han army got away.

sentences.zh: 藥元福曰：「劉崇悉發其眾，挾明騎而來，志吞晉、絳。

translations.literal: Yao Yuanfu said: "Liu Chong mobilized his entire force, brought Ming's cavalry with him, and came with the intent to swallow Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanfu said, "Liu Chong called up every man he had and marched here with the Khitan emperor Ming's cavalry, bent on swallowing Jin and Jiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 今氣衰力憊，狼狽而遁。

translations.literal: Now their spirit is spent and their strength exhausted; they flee in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Now their spirit is broken and their strength spent—they are fleeing in disorder.

sentences.zh: 不乘此翦撲，必為後患。

translations.literal: If we do not seize this moment to cut them down, they will surely become a later calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not cut them down now, they will surely trouble us again.

sentences.zh: 」諸將不欲進，王峻復遣使止之，遂還。

translations.literal: " The generals did not wish to advance; Wang Jun again sent a messenger to stop them, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals refused to go on. Wang Jun sent another order to halt the pursuit, and they turned back.

sentences.zh: 契丹比至晉陽，士馬什喪三四。

translations.literal: By the time the Khitan reached Jinyang, three or four tenths of their men and horses were lost.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Khitan reached Jinyang, they had lost three or four men and horses in ten.

sentences.zh: 蕭禹厥恥於無功，釘大酋長一人於市，旬餘而斬之。

translations.literal: Ashamed at achieving nothing, Xiao Yujue nailed a great chieftain in the marketplace; after more than ten days he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of returning empty-handed, Xiao Yujue had a senior chieftain nailed up in the marketplace and, more than ten days later, beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 北漢主始息意於進取。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler at last set aside his intent to advance and seize territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Han ruler at last abandoned his plans for further conquest.

sentences.zh: 北漢土瘠民貧，內供軍國，外奉契丹，賦繁役重，民不聊生，逃入周境者甚眾。

translations.literal: Northern Han's land was poor and its people impoverished; within they supplied the army and state, without they paid tribute to the Khitan—taxes were heavy and corvée burdens severe, the people could not live, and very many fled into Zhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Han was a land of thin soil and poor people. At home they had to sustain army and state; abroad they paid tribute to the Khitan. Taxes were crushing and labor demands relentless. Life became unbearable, and great numbers fled into Later Zhou territory.

sentences.zh: 唐主以鎮南節度使兼中書令宋齊丘為太傅，以馬希萼為江南西道觀察使、守中書令，鎮洪州，仍賜爵楚王。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler made Song Qiqiu, military governor of Zhennan and concurrent director of the Secretariat, grand tutor; he made Ma Xie'e Jiangnan West Circuit observer, retaining director of the Secretariat, stationed at Hong Prefecture, and still granted him the title King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor made Song Qiqiu, military governor of Zhennan and concurrent director of the Secretariat, grand tutor. He appointed Ma Xie'e observer of the Jiangnan West Circuit, retaining the title of director of the Secretariat, with his seat at Hong Prefecture, and still granted him the rank of King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 以馬希崇為永泰節度使、兼侍中，鎮舒州。

translations.literal: He made Ma Xiechong military governor of Yongtai and concurrent palace attendant, stationed at Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He made Ma Xiechong military governor of Yongtai and concurrent palace attendant, with his seat at Shu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 湖南將吏，位高者拜刺史、將軍、卿監，卑者以次拜官。

translations.literal: Hunan's generals and officials of high rank were appointed prefects, generals, and supervisory commissioners; those of lower rank received appointments in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The senior generals and officials of Hunan were given posts as prefects, generals, and supervisory commissioners; junior men received appointments in descending order.

sentences.zh: 唐主嘉廖偃、彭師暠之忠，以偃為左殿直軍使、萊州刺史，師暠為殿直都虞候，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler commended Liao Yan and Peng Shigao for their loyalty; he made Yan left palace direct army commissioner and prefect of Lai, and Shigao direct army chief adjutant, with very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor rewarded Liao Yan and Peng Shigao for their loyalty. Yan was made left palace direct army commissioner and prefect of Lai; Shigao was made direct army chief adjutant. Both received lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 湖南刺史皆入朝於唐，永州刺史王贇獨後至，唐王毒殺之。

translations.literal: The Hunan prefects all came to court in Tang; only Yong Prefecture prefect Wang Yun arrived late, and the Tang ruler poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan prefects all presented themselves at the Southern Tang court; only Wang Yun of Yong Prefecture came late, and the Southern Tang emperor had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 南漢主遣內侍省丞潘崇徹、將軍謝貫將兵攻郴州，唐邊鎬發兵救之。

translations.literal: The Southern Han ruler dispatched Inner Palace Bureau deputy Pan Chongche and general Xie Guan to lead troops to attack Chen Prefecture; Tang's Bian Hao sent troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Han emperor sent Inner Palace Bureau deputy Pan Chongche and general Xie Guan to attack Chen Prefecture; Bian Hao of Southern Tang marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 崇徹敗唐兵於義章，遂取郴州。

translations.literal: Chongche defeated Tang troops at Yizhang and then took Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chongche routed the Southern Tang army at Yizhang and then seized Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 邊鎬請除全、道二州刺史以備南漢。

translations.literal: Bian Hao requested that the prefects of Quan and Dao be removed and replaced to guard against Southern Han.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao asked that new prefects be appointed at Quan and Dao to guard against Southern Han.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，唐主以廖偃為道州刺史，以黑雲指揮使張巒知全州。

translations.literal: On bingchen the Tang ruler made Liao Yan prefect of Dao and Black Cloud Commander Zhang Luan acting prefect of Quan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the Southern Tang emperor made Liao Yan prefect of Dao and Black Cloud Commander Zhang Luan acting prefect of Quan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，唐主以安化節度使鄱陽王王延政為山南西道節度使，更賜爵光山王。

translations.literal: That year the Tang ruler made Wang Yanzheng, military governor of Anhua and Prince of Poyang, military governor of the Shannan West Circuit and further granted him the title Prince of Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Southern Tang emperor made Wang Yanzheng, military governor of Anhua and Prince of Poyang, military governor of the Shannan West Circuit and raised his title to Prince of Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 初，蒙城鎮將鹹師朗將部兵降唐，唐主以其兵為奉節都，從邊鎬平湖南。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mengcheng garrison commander Xian Shilang led his troops in surrender to Tang; the Tang ruler made his soldiers the Fengjie Command and had them follow Bian Hao in pacifying Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Mengcheng garrison commander Xian Shilang had surrendered with his troops to Southern Tang. The emperor enrolled them as the Fengjie Command and sent them with Bian Hao to pacify Hunan.

sentences.zh: 唐悉收湖南金帛、珍玩、倉粟乃至舟艦、亭館、花果之美者，皆徙於金陵，遣都官郎中楊繼勳等收湖南租賦以贍戍兵。

translations.literal: Tang thoroughly collected Hunan's gold and silk, precious curios, granary stores, and even fine boats, pavilions, flowers, and fruit—all were moved to Jinling; they dispatched Ministry of Justice bureau director Yang Jixun and others to collect Hunan's rents and taxes to supply the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang stripped Hunan of its gold and silk, precious objects, and stored grain, and even its finest boats, pavilions, gardens, and orchards—all were hauled off to Jinling. Yang Jixun of the Ministry of Justice and others were sent to levy Hunan's taxes to pay the occupying troops.

sentences.zh: 繼勳等務為苛刻，湖南人失望。

translations.literal: Jixun and the others strove to be harsh; the people of Hunan were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun and his colleagues squeezed every penny they could, and the people of Hunan lost heart.

sentences.zh: 行營糧料使王紹顏減士卒糧賜，奉節指揮使孫朗、曹進怒曰：「昔吾從鹹公降唐，唐待我豈如今日湖南將士之厚哉！

translations.literal: Field provisions commissioner Wang Shaoyan reduced the soldiers' grain rations and stipends; Fengjie commander Sun Lang and Cao Jin said in anger: "In the past when we followed Lord Xian in surrendering to Tang, how could Tang's treatment of us compare with how Hunan's officers and soldiers are treated today!
translations.idiomatic: Field provisions commissioner Wang Shaoyan cut the troops' grain rations and pay. Fengjie commander Sun Lang and Cao Jin said angrily, "When we followed Lord Xian in surrendering to Southern Tang, we were treated far better than Hunan's officers and soldiers are treated now!

sentences.zh: 今有功不增祿賜，又減之，不如殺紹顏及鎬，據湖南，歸中原，富貴可圖也！

translations.literal: Now merit brings no increase in salary or gifts, yet they are reduced—better to kill Shaoyan and Hao, hold Hunan, and return to the Central Plains; wealth and honor can be grasped!
translations.idiomatic: We have won victories yet receive no raise in pay or rewards—only cuts. Better to kill Shaoyan and Hao, seize Hunan, and go back to the Central Plains. Fortune and rank would be within reach!

sentences.zh: 春正月庚申，夜，孫朗、曹進帥其徒作亂，束蒿潛燒府門，火不然。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring, on gengshen at night, Sun Lang and Cao Jin led their followers in mutiny; they bound reeds and secretly tried to burn the prefectural gate, but the fire would not catch.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of gengshen in the first month of spring, Sun Lang and Cao Jin led their men in revolt. They bound reeds and tried to set fire to the prefectural gate in secret, but the flames would not take.

sentences.zh: 邊鎬覺之，出兵格鬥，且命鳴鼓角，朗、進等以為將曉，斬關奔朗州。

translations.literal: Bian Hao detected it, sent troops out to grapple with them, and also ordered drums and horns sounded; Lang, Jin, and the others thought dawn was near, cut through the gate, and fled to Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao discovered the plot, sent troops out to fight them, and ordered drums and horns sounded. Lang and Jin, thinking daybreak was near, broke through the gate and fled to Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王逵問朗曰：「吾昔從武穆王，與淮南戰屢捷，淮南兵易與耳。

translations.literal: Wang Kui asked Lang: "In the past when I followed Prince Wumu, we fought the Huai region many times and won repeatedly; Huainan troops are easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui asked Lang, "When I followed Prince Wumu, we fought the Huai region again and again and always won. Huainan armies are easy meat.

sentences.zh: 今欲以朗州之眾復取湖南，可乎？

translations.literal: Now I wish to use the forces of Lang Prefecture to recover Hunan—is it possible?"
translations.idiomatic: Can we use Lang Prefecture's forces to take Hunan back?"

sentences.zh: 」朗曰：「朗在金陵數年，備見其政事，朝無賢臣，軍無良將，忠佞無別，賞罰不當，如此，得國存幸矣，何暇兼人！

translations.literal: Lang said: "Lang was in Jinling for several years and saw their government in full: at court there are no worthy ministers, in the army no good generals, loyal and treacherous are not distinguished, rewards and punishments are not fitting—given this, merely keeping the state alive is good fortune; how could there be leisure to swallow others!
translations.idiomatic: Lang said, "I spent years in Jinling and saw their government close up. The court has no worthy ministers, the army no able generals, loyalty and treachery go undistinguished, and rewards and punishments miss their mark. A state like that is lucky merely to survive—what leisure has it to swallow others!

sentences.zh: 朗請為公前驅，取湖南如拾芥耳！

translations.literal: Lang asks to go before you as vanguard; taking Hunan would be like picking up a mustard seed!
translations.idiomatic: Let me lead the way for you—taking Hunan back would be like picking up a mustard seed from the ground!

sentences.zh: 」逵悅，厚遇之。

translations.literal: " Kui was pleased and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was delighted and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，發開封府民夫五萬修大梁城，旬日而罷。

translations.literal: On renxu corvée laborers from the Kaifeng prefecture, fifty thousand in number, were mobilized to repair the walls of Daliang; in ten days the work ceased.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu fifty thousand corvée laborers from Kaifeng Prefecture were pressed to repair the walls of Daliang; the work was finished in ten days.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超發鄉兵入城，引泗水注壕中，為戰守之備。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao mobilized local militia into the city, diverted the Si River to fill the moat, and made preparations for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao called local militia into the city, diverted the Si River to fill the moat, and made ready for siege and defense.

sentences.zh: 又多以旗幟授諸鎮將，令募群盜，剽掠鄰境，所在奏其反狀。

translations.literal: He also gave many banners and flags to garrison commanders and ordered them to recruit bandit gangs to plunder neighboring circuits; everywhere memorials reported their rebellious conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He also handed out banners and flags to garrison commanders and ordered them to recruit outlaw bands to raid neighboring circuits, so that reports of rebellion poured in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 甲子，敕沂、密二州不復隸泰寧軍。

translations.literal: On jiazi an edict declared that Yi and Mi prefectures would no longer be subordinate to the Taining army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi an edict removed Yi and Mi prefectures from the jurisdiction of the Taining army.

sentences.zh: 以侍衛步軍都指揮使、昭武節度使曹英為都部署，討彥超，齊州防禦使史延超為副部署，皇城使河內向訓為都監，陳州防禦使樂元福為行營馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: Palace guard infantry commander and Zhaowu military governor Cao Ying was made overall commander to suppress Yanchao; Qi Prefecture defense commissioner Shi Yanchao was deputy commander; Imperial City commissioner Xiang Xun of Henei was overall supervisor; Chen Prefecture defense commissioner Yue Yuanfu was field army cavalry and infantry chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ying, palace guard infantry commander and military governor of Zhaowu, was made overall commander to suppress Yanchao. Shi Yanchao, defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture, was deputy commander; Xiang Xun of Henei, imperial city commissioner, was overall supervisor; and Yue Yuanfu, defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture, was field army cavalry and infantry chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 帝以元福宿將，命英、訓無得以軍禮見之，二人皆父事之。

translations.literal: Because Yuanfu was a veteran general, the emperor ordered Ying and Xun not to receive him with military ceremony; both treated him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuanfu was a veteran general, the emperor ordered Ying and Xun not to stand on military ceremony with him; both treated him with a son's deference.

sentences.zh: 唐主發兵五千，軍於下邳，以援彥超。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler dispatched five thousand troops, encamped at Xiapi, to aid Yanchao.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor sent five thousand troops to Xiapi to aid Yanchao.

sentences.zh: 聞周兵將至，退屯沐陽。

translations.literal: Hearing Zhou troops were about to arrive, they withdrew and encamped at Muyang.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard Zhou forces were approaching, they fell back and encamped at Muyang.

sentences.zh: 徐州巡檢使張令彬擊之，大破唐兵，殺、溺死者千餘人，獲其將燕敬權。

translations.literal: Xuzhou inspection commissioner Zhang Lingbin attacked them, routed Tang troops, killed and drowned more than a thousand men, and captured their general Yan Jingquan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou inspection commissioner Zhang Lingbin struck them, shattered the Southern Tang army, killed or drowned more than a thousand men, and captured their general Yan Jingquan.

sentences.zh: 初，彥超以周室新造，謂其易搖，故北召北漢及契丹，南誘唐人，使侵邊鄙，冀朝廷奔命不暇，然後乘間而動。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yanchao, because the Zhou house was newly founded, thought it easy to shake; therefore he summoned Northern Han and the Khitan in the north and enticed the Tang in the south to invade the borders, hoping the court would be too busy rushing to emergencies and he could then seize an opening to act.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao had judged the newly founded Zhou regime unstable. He had called in Northern Han and the Khitan from the north and incited Southern Tang from the south to raid the borders, hoping the court would be driven to distraction and he could strike at his moment.

sentences.zh: 及北漢、契丹自晉州北走，唐兵敗於沐陽，彥超之勢遂沮。

translations.literal: When Northern Han and the Khitan fled north from Jin Prefecture and Tang troops were defeated at Muyang, Yanchao's momentum was checked.
translations.idiomatic: But Northern Han and the Khitan had fled north from Jin Prefecture, and the Southern Tang army had been broken at Muyang—Yanchao's momentum collapsed.

sentences.zh: 永興節度使李洪信，自以漢室近親，心不自安。

translations.literal: Yongxing military governor Li Hongxin, considering himself a close kinsman of the Han house, was uneasy in his own mind.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongxin, military governor of Yongxing, counted himself a close kinsman of the fallen Han dynasty and lived in private unease.

sentences.zh: 城中兵不滿千人，王峻在陝，以救晉州為名，發其數百。

translations.literal: The troops in the city numbered fewer than a thousand; Wang Jun was in Shan and, under the pretext of rescuing Jin Prefecture, mobilized several hundred of them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison in his city numbered fewer than a thousand men. Wang Jun, then in Shan Prefecture, had already drawn off several hundred of them on the pretext of relieving Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及北漢兵遁去，遣禁兵千餘人戍長安。

translations.literal: When Northern Han troops had fled away, he dispatched more than a thousand palace troops to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After the Northern Han army withdrew, Jun sent more than a thousand palace troops to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 洪信懼，遂入朝。

translations.literal: Hongxin was afraid and thereupon came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin was terrified and came to court in person.

sentences.zh: 壬申，王峻自晉州還，入見。

translations.literal: On renshen Wang Jun returned from Jin Prefecture and entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Wang Jun returned from Jin Prefecture and was received in audience.

sentences.zh: 曹英等至兗州，設長圍。

translations.literal: Cao Ying and the others reached Yan Prefecture and established a long encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ying and the others reached Yan Prefecture and drew a tight cordon around the city.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超屢出戰，藥元福皆擊敗之，彥超不敢出。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao sallied forth to fight many times; Yao Yuanfu defeated him each time, and Yanchao did not dare come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao sallied out again and again; Yao Yuanfu beat him back every time until Yanchao no longer dared leave the walls.

sentences.zh: 十餘日，長圍合，遂進攻之。

translations.literal: After more than ten days the long encirclement closed; they then pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days the ring closed tight, and the assault began in earnest.

sentences.zh: 初，彥超將反，判官崔周度諫曰：「魯，詩書之國，自伯禽以來不能霸諸侯，然以禮義守之，可以長世。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanchao was about to rebel, aide Cui Zhoudu remonstrated: "Lu is a land of the Odes and Documents; since Duke Boqin it has never dominated the feudal lords, yet by guarding it with ritual and righteousness one may long endure.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanchao was first plotting rebellion, his aide Cui Zhoudu warned him, "Lu is a land of the Odes and Documents. Since Duke Boqin it has never dominated the feudal lords, yet by holding it with ritual and righteousness a house may endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 公於國家非有私憾，胡為自疑！

translations.literal: You bear no private grievance against the state—why doubt yourself!
translations.idiomatic: You have no private quarrel with the throne—why turn against yourself!

sentences.zh: 況主上開諭勤至，苟撤備歸誠，則坐享泰山之安矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the sovereign's admonitions have been earnest and thorough; if you lay down your guard and return in loyalty, you will sit and enjoy the security of Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's appeals have been earnest and repeated. Lay down your arms, submit in good faith, and you will sit secure as Mount Tai itself.

sentences.zh: 獨不見杜中令、安襄陽、李河中竟何所成乎！

translations.literal: Have you alone not seen what Chancellor Du, An of Xiangyang, and Li of Hezhong finally achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen what became of Chancellor Du, An of Xiangyang, and Li of Hezhong in the end?

sentences.zh: 」彥超怒。

translations.literal: " Yanchao was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 及官軍圍城，彥超括士民之財以贍軍，坐匿財死者甚眾。

translations.literal: When the imperial army besieged the city, Yanchao levied the property of scholars and commoners to supply the army; very many were put to death for concealing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army besieged the city, Yanchao extorted the wealth of gentry and commoners alike to feed his troops. Many who were accused of hiding property were put to death.

sentences.zh: 前陝州司馬閻弘魯，寶之子也，畏彥超之暴，傾家為獻。

translations.literal: Former Shan Prefecture aide Yan Honglu, son of Bao, feared Yanchao's cruelty and emptied his household in offering tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Honglu, former aide of Shan Prefecture and son of Yan Bao, terrified by Yanchao's brutality, stripped his household bare in tribute.

sentences.zh: 彥超猶以為有所匿，命周度索其家，周度謂弘魯曰：「君之死生，系財之豐約，宜無所愛。

translations.literal: Yanchao still thought he was hiding something and ordered Zhoudu to search his home; Zhoudu said to Honglu: "Your life or death hangs on the abundance or scarcity of your wealth—you should hold nothing back."
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao still suspected concealment and ordered Zhoudu to search his home. Zhoudu told Honglu, "Your life depends on how much wealth you surrender—you must hold nothing back."

sentences.zh: 」弘魯泣拜其妻妾曰：「悉出所有以救吾死。

translations.literal: Honglu wept and bowed to his wife and concubines, saying: "Bring out everything you have to save my life."
translations.idiomatic: Honglu wept and bowed to his wife and concubines. "Give up everything we have to save my life," he said.

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「竭矣！

translations.literal: They all said: "It is exhausted!"
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "There is nothing left!"

sentences.zh: 」周度以白彥超，彥超不信，收弘魯夫妻繫獄。

translations.literal: Zhoudu reported this to Yanchao; Yanchao did not believe it and imprisoned Honglu and his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoudu reported this to Yanchao, but Yanchao refused to believe it and had Honglu and his wife thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 有乳母於泥中掊得金纏臂，獻之，冀以贖其主。

translations.literal: A wet nurse dug up a gold armlet from the mud and presented it, hoping thereby to ransom her master.
translations.idiomatic: A wet nurse dug a gold armlet out of the mud and offered it up, hoping to buy her master's life.

sentences.zh: 彥超曰：「果然，所匿必猶多。

translations.literal: Yanchao said: "As expected—what is hidden must still be very much."
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao said, "Just as I thought—there must be far more hidden away."

sentences.zh: 」榜掠弘魯夫妻，肉潰而死。

translations.literal: He had Honglu and his wife beaten until their flesh split open and they died.
translations.idiomatic: He had Honglu and his wife flogged until their flesh gave way and they died.

sentences.zh: 以周度為阿庇，斬於市。

translations.literal: He treated Zhoudu as one who had shielded Honglu and beheaded him in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He condemned Zhoudu as an accomplice who had shielded Honglu and had him beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 北漢遣兵寇府州，防禦使折德扆敗之，殺二千餘人。

translations.literal: Northern Han dispatched troops to raid Fu Prefecture; defense commissioner Zhe Deyi defeated them and killed more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Han sent troops to raid Fu Prefecture. Defense commissioner Zhe Deyi routed them and killed more than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚子，德扆奏攻拔北漢岢嵐軍，以兵戍之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengzi, Deyi memorialized that he had attacked and captured Northern Han's Ke Lan garrison and garrisoned it with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengzi, Deyi reported that he had stormed and taken Northern Han's Ke Lan garrison and left troops to hold it.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，帝釋燕敬權等使歸唐，謂唐主曰：「叛臣，天下所共疾也，不意唐主助之，得無非計乎！

translations.literal: On jiachen the emperor released Yan Jingquan and the others and sent them back to Tang, saying to the Tang ruler: "Rebellious ministers are hated by all under Heaven— I did not expect the Tang ruler to aid them; can this be anything but a bad plan!"
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the emperor released Yan Jingquan and the others and sent them back to Southern Tang with a message for its ruler: "Rebellious ministers are despised throughout the realm. I never expected the Southern Tang emperor to aid one. Surely that cannot have been wise counsel!"

sentences.zh: 」唐主大慚，先所得中國人，皆禮而歸之。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was greatly ashamed; all Chinese he had previously taken he treated with courtesy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor was deeply shamed. Every subject of the Central Plains he had held captive was treated with courtesy and sent home.

sentences.zh: 唐之言事者猶獻取中原之策，中書舍人韓熙載曰：「郭氏有國雖淺，為治已固，我兵輕動，必有害無益。

translations.literal: Tang's policy advisers still offered plans to seize the Central Plains; Secretariat drafter Han Xizai said: "Although the Guo house's possession of the realm is shallow, its governance is already firm—if our troops move lightly, there will surely be harm and no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang advisers still urged schemes to seize the Central Plains. Secretariat drafter Han Xizai said, "The Guo regime may be young, but its rule is already solid. If we stir our armies lightly, we will only hurt ourselves."

sentences.zh: 唐自烈祖以來，常遣使泛海與契丹相結，欲與之共製中國，更相饋遺，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Since the time of the Tang's Liezu, they had often dispatched envoys by sea to join with the Khitan, wishing together to control the Central Plains; they exchanged gifts back and forth and pledged brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reign of Southern Tang's founding emperor, envoys had crossed the sea again and again to treat with the Khitan, hoping to join forces against the Central Plains. Gifts passed back and forth and oaths of brotherhood were exchanged.

sentences.zh: 然契丹利其貨，徒以虛語往來，實不為唐用也。

translations.literal: Yet the Khitan coveted their goods; they merely exchanged empty words and in fact did not act for Tang's use.
translations.idiomatic: But the Khitan cared only for Southern Tang's treasure. The talk flowed freely, yet in deed they never served Southern Tang's ends.

sentences.zh: 唐主好文學，故熙載與馮延己、延魯、江文蔚、潘佐、徐鉉之徒皆至美官。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler loved literature; therefore Xizai, Feng Yanji, Yanlu, Jiang Wenwei, Pan Zuo, Xu Xuan, and men like them all reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor loved letters, and so Xizai, Feng Yanji, Yanlu, Jiang Wenwei, Pan Zuo, Xu Xuan, and others like them all rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 佑，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Zuo was a man of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was a native of You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 當時唐之文雅於諸國為盛，然未嘗設科舉，多因上書言事拜官，至是，始命韓林學士江文蔚知貢舉，進士廬陵王克貞等三人及第。

translations.literal: At that time Tang's literary refinement among the various states was the most flourishing, yet they had never established the civil service examinations; many received office through submitting memorials on affairs of state—now at last they ordered Hanlin academician Jiang Wenwei to supervise the examinations, and three men including jinshi Wang Kezhen of Luling passed.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang culture then outshone every neighboring state, yet it had never held civil examinations; most offices came through memorials on public affairs. Now, for the first time, Hanlin academician Jiang Wenwei was ordered to supervise the examinations, and three candidates including jinshi Wang Kezhen of Luling passed.

sentences.zh: 唐主問文蔚：「聊取士何如前朝？

translations.literal: The Tang ruler asked Wenwei: "How does selecting scholars this time compare with the previous dynasty?"
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor asked Wenwei, "How does this round of selecting scholars compare with the previous dynasty?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「前朝公舉、私謁相半，臣專任至公耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "In the previous dynasty public recommendation and private solicitation were half and half; your servant has relied solely on utmost fairness."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Under the previous dynasty public recommendation and private solicitation were evenly mixed. I have relied on nothing but absolute fairness."

sentences.zh: 」唐主悅。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人張緯，前朝登第，聞而銜之。

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter Zhang Wei, who had passed the examinations under the previous dynasty, heard this and resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Zhang Wei, who had passed the examinations under the previous dynasty, took offense.

sentences.zh: 時執政皆不由科第，相與沮毀，竟罷貢舉。

translations.literal: At the time those holding power had none come through the examinations; they together obstructed and slandered, and in the end the examinations were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The men then in power had none risen through the examinations. They joined in obstruction and slander until the examinations were abolished altogether.

sentences.zh: 三月戊辰，以內客省使、恩州團練使晉陽鄭仁誨為樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuchen, Inner Palace Bureau commissioner and En Prefecture training commissioner Zheng Renhui of Jinyang was made deputy commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuchen, Inner Palace Bureau commissioner and training commissioner of En Prefecture Zheng Renhui of Jinyang was made deputy commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，改威勝軍曰武勝軍。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the Weisheng army was renamed the Wusheng army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the Weisheng army was renamed the Wusheng army.

sentences.zh: 唐主以太弟太保、昭義節度使馮延己為左僕射，前鎮海節度使徐景運為中書侍郎，及右僕射孫晟皆同平章事。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler appointed his younger brother's Grand Guardian and Zhaoyi military commissioner Feng Yanji as Left Vice Director, former Zhenhai military commissioner Xu Jingyun as Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Right Vice Director Sun Sheng—all as Fellow Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor made his younger brother's Grand Guardian and Zhaoyi military commissioner Feng Yanji Left Vice Director, former Zhenhai military commissioner Xu Jingyun Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Right Vice Director Sun Sheng—all fellow grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 既宣制，戶部尚書常夢錫眾中大言曰：「白麻甚佳，但不及江文蔚疏耳！

translations.literal: When the appointment edict was proclaimed, Minister of Revenue Chang Mengxi spoke loudly before the assembly, saying: "The white hemp edict is very fine, but it does not match Jiang Wenwei's memorial!"
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the appointment was announced, Minister of Revenue Chang Mengxi cried out before the whole court: "A handsome edict on white hemp—but it still falls short of Jiang Wenwei's memorial!"

sentences.zh: 」晟素輕延己，謂人曰：「金盃玉碗，乃貯狗矢乎！

translations.literal: Sheng had always looked down on Yanji and said to others: "Are gold cups and jade bowls meant to store dog droppings!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng had long despised Feng Yanji and told others, "Gold cups and jade bowls—to hold dog shit?"

sentences.zh: 」延己言於唐主曰：「陛下躬親庶務，故宰相不得盡其才，此治道所以未成也。

translations.literal: Yanji said to the Tang ruler: "Your Majesty personally attends to every detail of government, so the chief councilors cannot fully employ their talents—this is why the way of good governance has not yet been achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji told the Southern Tang emperor, "Your Majesty handles every detail of government yourself, so your chief councilors never get to use their full abilities. That is why sound rule still eludes us."

sentences.zh: 」唐主乃悉以政事委之，奏可而已。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler then entrusted all government affairs to them, merely approving their submissions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon handed over the whole administration to them, content to ratify whatever they put before him.

sentences.zh: 既而延己不能勤事，文書皆仰成胥史，軍旅則委之邊將。

translations.literal: Before long Yanji could not attend diligently to affairs; documents all relied on clerks to finish, and military matters were delegated to frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Feng Yanji stopped doing the work himself. Paperwork was left to clerks to finish as they could, and army business went entirely to the border commanders.

sentences.zh: 頃之，事益不治，唐主乃復自覽之。

translations.literal: Before long affairs grew ever more poorly managed, and the Tang ruler again began to review them himself.
translations.idiomatic: In short order government grew worse, and the Southern Tang emperor took the files back into his own hands.

sentences.zh: 大理卿蕭儼惡延己為人，數上疏攻之，會儼坐失入人死罪，鐘謨、李德明輩必欲殺之，延己曰：「儼誤殺一婦人，諸君以為當死，儼九卿也，可誤殺乎？

translations.literal: Grand Justice of the Court Xiao Yan detested Yanji's character and repeatedly submitted memorials attacking him. When Yan happened to be convicted of wrongly imposing the death penalty, Zhong Mo, Li Deming, and their faction insisted he must die. Yanji said: "Yan mistakenly killed one woman—you gentlemen think he should die. Yan is a minister of the Nine Ministers—may one mistakenly kill him?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Justice Xiao Yan loathed Feng Yanji and kept memorializing against him. When Yan was convicted of wrongly condemning someone to death, Zhong Mo, Li Deming, and their allies demanded his execution. Feng Yanji said, "Yan mistakenly killed one woman, and you think he should die for it? He is a minister of the Nine Ministers—are ministers to be killed by mistake?"

sentences.zh: 」獨上言：「儼素有直聲，今所坐已會赦，宜從寬宥。

translations.literal: He alone submitted a statement: "Yan has long enjoyed a reputation for integrity; the offense for which he now stands has already been covered by amnesty—he should be treated with lenient pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji alone pleaded, "Yan has long been known for his integrity, and the crime he stands convicted of is already covered by the amnesty. He should be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 」儼由是得免。

translations.literal: Yan thereby escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan was spared.

sentences.zh: 人亦以此多之。

translations.literal: People also on this account praised Yanji.
translations.idiomatic: The public praised Feng Yanji for it.

sentences.zh: 景運尋罷為太子少傅。

translations.literal: Jingyun was soon dismissed and made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingyun was soon removed from office and made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingxu, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on bingxu—the first day of the month—the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 帝以曹英等攻克兗州久未克，乙卯，下詔親征，以李穀權東京留守兼判開封府，鄭仁誨權大內都點檢，又以侍衛馬軍都指揮使郭崇充在京都巡檢。

translations.literal: Because Cao Ying and the others had attacked Yan Prefecture for a long time without taking it, on yimao the emperor issued an edict for a personal campaign. He made Li Gu acting Eastern Capital regent and concurrent administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture, Zheng Renhui acting chief inspector of the Inner Palace, and also appointed Palace Attendant Horse Army commander Guo Chong to patrol the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ying's forces had besieged Yanzhou for months without success. On yimao the emperor announced he would lead the campaign in person. Li Gu was left as acting regent at the Eastern Capital and concurrent administrator of Kaifeng; Zheng Renhui was made acting chief inspector of the Inner Palace; and Palace Attendant Horse Army commander Guo Chong was ordered to patrol the capital.

sentences.zh: 唐主既克湖南，遣其將李建期屯益陽以圖朗州，以知全州張巒兼桂州招討使以圖桂州，久之，未有功。

translations.literal: After the Tang ruler had conquered Hunan, he sent his general Li Jianqi to garrison Yiyang to target Lang Prefecture, and made Quan Prefecture prefect Zhang Luan also commissioner for suppressing Gui Prefecture to target Gui Prefecture. After a long time there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering Hunan, the Southern Tang emperor posted his general Li Jianqi at Yiyang to threaten Langzhou and made Quanzhou prefect Zhang Luan also commissioner for the Guizhou campaign. Months passed without result.

sentences.zh: 唐主謂馮延己、孫晟曰：「楚人求息肩於我，我未有以撫其瘡痍而虐用其力，非所以副來蘇之望。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler said to Feng Yanji and Sun Sheng: "The people of Chu seek to rest their shoulders upon us, yet we have not healed their wounds and instead exhaust their strength—this does not fulfill the hope that they would revive under our rule."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor told Feng Yanji and Sun Sheng, "The people of Chu came to us hoping for relief, yet we have not tended their wounds and instead work them to exhaustion. That is no way to answer their hope of revival under our rule."

sentences.zh: 吾欲罷桂林之役，斂益陽之戍，以旌節授劉言，何如？

translations.literal: I wish to halt the Guilin campaign, withdraw the garrison at Yiyang, and invest Liu Yan with a staff of authority—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I want to call off the Guilin expedition, pull back the garrison at Yiyang, and invest Liu Yan with a commander's staff. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」晟以為宜然。

translations.literal: Sheng thought it should be so.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 延己曰：「吾出偏將舉湖南，遠近震驚。

translations.literal: Yanji said: "When we sent out a subordinate general and took Hunan, near and far were shaken with alarm."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji said, "We sent a subordinate general and seized Hunan—the whole region trembled."

sentences.zh: 一旦三分喪二，人將輕我。

translations.literal: If in one day we lose two-thirds of it, people will look down on us.
translations.idiomatic: If we surrender two-thirds of it in a single stroke, everyone will think less of us.

sentences.zh: 請委邊將察其形勢。

translations.literal: I ask that frontier generals be entrusted to observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Let the frontier commanders read the situation and decide.

sentences.zh: 」唐主乃遣統軍使侯訓將兵五千自吉州路趣全州，與張巒合兵攻桂州。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler then sent army commander Hou Xun leading five thousand troops by the Ji Prefecture route toward Quan Prefecture to join Zhang Luan's forces in attacking Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang emperor instead sent army commander Hou Xun with five thousand men by way of Jizhou toward Quanzhou to join Zhang Luan for an assault on Guilin.

sentences.zh: 南漢伏兵於山谷，巒等始至城下，罷乏，伏兵四起，城中出兵夾擊之，唐兵大敗，訓死，巒收散卒數百奔歸全州。

translations.literal: Southern Han laid ambushes in the valleys. When Luan and the others had just reached below the city wall, exhausted, the ambushers rose on all sides, troops sallied from the city to strike from both flanks, and the Tang army was utterly defeated. Xun died; Luan gathered several hundred scattered soldiers and fled back to Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Han hid troops in the mountain valleys. When Zhang Luan's men had just reached the foot of the walls, worn out, ambushers sprang up everywhere and the garrison sallied to hit them from both sides. The Southern Tang army was routed. Hou Xun was killed; Zhang Luan rallied a few hundred survivors and fled back to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚申，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengshen, the emperor departed from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengshen, the emperor left Daliang.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，至兗州。

translations.literal: On wuchen he reached Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he arrived at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 己巳，帝使人招諭慕容彥超，城上人語不遜。

translations.literal: On jisi the emperor sent men to summon and instruct Murong Yanchao; those on the wall replied insolently.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor sent envoys to summon Murong Yanchao and offer terms; the men on the walls answered with insults.

sentences.zh: 庚午，命諸軍進攻。

translations.literal: On gengwu he ordered the armies to advance the attack.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he ordered a general assault.

sentences.zh: 先是，術者紿彥超云：「鎮星行至角、亢，角、亢兗州之分，其下有福。

translations.literal: Earlier, a diviner had deceived Yanchao, saying: "The Seat Star is passing through the Horn and Gullet—Horn and Gullet are Yan Prefecture's allotted region; below them there is blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a fortune-teller had tricked Yanchao, saying, "Saturn is moving through the Horn and Gullet—Yanzhou falls under those asterisms, and fortune waits beneath them."

sentences.zh: 」彥超乃立祠而禱之，令民家皆立黃幡。

translations.literal: Yanchao thereupon erected a shrine and prayed to it, ordering every household to raise yellow banners.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao built a shrine to Saturn and prayed there, ordering every household to fly yellow banners.

sentences.zh: 彥超性貪吝，官軍攻城急，猶瘞藏珍寶，由是人無鬥志，將卒相繼有出降者。

translations.literal: Yanchao was by nature greedy and stingy. Though the imperial army pressed the siege hard, he still buried his treasures, and on this account the people had no fighting spirit; officers and soldiers one after another came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao was miserly by nature. Even as the siege tightened, he kept burying his treasure, and morale collapsed. Officers and soldiers surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，官軍克城，彥超方禱鎮星祠，帥眾力戰，不勝，乃焚鎮星祠，與妻赴井死。

translations.literal: On yihai the imperial army took the city. Yanchao was just then praying at the Seat Star shrine, led his men in a desperate fight, could not prevail, then burned the Seat Star shrine, and with his wife threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the imperial army broke into the city. Murong Yanchao was still at prayer in the Saturn shrine when he led a last stand, failed, burned the shrine, and threw himself into a well with his wife.

sentences.zh: 子繼勳出走，追獲，殺之。

translations.literal: His son Jixun fled; he was pursued, captured, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Jixun tried to flee, was caught, and executed.

sentences.zh: 官軍大掠，城中死者近萬人。

translations.literal: The imperial army plundered on a great scale; nearly ten thousand people died in the city.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial troops looted the city on a vast scale. Nearly ten thousand people died.

sentences.zh: 初，彥超將反，募群盜置帳下，至者二千餘人，皆山林獷悍，竟不為用。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanchao was about to rebel, he recruited bandits and placed them under his command—more than two thousand came, all fierce men of mountain forests, yet in the end they proved useless.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Yanchao had first plotted rebellion he recruited more than two thousand bandits—hard men from the hills—but in the end they did him no good at all.

sentences.zh: 帝欲悉誅兗州將吏，翰林學士竇儀見馮道、范質，與之共白帝曰：「彼皆脅從耳。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to execute all Yan Prefecture's officers and officials. Hanlin academician Dou Yi saw Feng Dao and Fan Zhi and together reported to the emperor, saying: "They were all coerced followers."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to put every Yanzhou officer and official to death. Hanlin academician Dou Yi sought out Feng Dao and Fan Zhi, and together they pleaded with the emperor: "They were only men forced to follow him."

sentences.zh: 」乃赦之。

translations.literal: They were thereupon pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以端明殿學士顏衎權知兗州事。

translations.literal: On dingchou Yan Kan, academician of the Duanming Hall, was appointed acting administrator of Yan Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Duanming Hall academician Yan Kan was made acting administrator of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬午，赦兗州管內，彥超黨與逃匿者期一月聽自首，前已伏誅者赦其親戚。

translations.literal: On renwu he proclaimed an amnesty within Yan Prefecture's jurisdiction; Yanchao's partisans in hiding were given one month to surrender themselves, and the kin of those already executed were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he declared an amnesty throughout Yanzhou. Yanchao's followers in hiding were given one month to turn themselves in, and the families of those already executed were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 癸未，降泰寧軍為防禦州。

translations.literal: On guimwei the Taining army was reduced to a defensive prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guimwei the Taining army was downgraded to a defensive prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐司徒致仕李建勳卒，且死，戒家人曰：「時事如此，吾得良死幸矣！

translations.literal: Tang's retired Grand Secretary Li Jianxun died. As death approached he admonished his family, saying: "Affairs are as they are—I am fortunate to die a good death!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianxun, retired Grand Secretary of Southern Tang, died. On his deathbed he told his family, "Times being what they are, I am lucky to die in my bed."

sentences.zh: 勿封土立碑，聽人耕種於其上，免為他日開發之標。

translations.literal: Do not mound earth or erect a stele; let people farm upon it, lest it become a marker for future looters.
translations.idiomatic: Do not raise a mound or set up a stele. Let people farm the ground above me, so no one can find the spot later and dig me up.

sentences.zh: 」及江南之亡也，諸貴人高大之塚無不發者，惟建勳塚莫知其處。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan fell, there was no great tomb of the nobility that was not opened—only Jianxun's tomb, no one knew where it was.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan fell, every great noble tomb was opened—only Li Jianxun's burial place remained unknown.

sentences.zh: 六月乙酉朔，帝如曲阜，謁孔子祠。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yiyou, the first day of the month, the emperor went to Qufu and visited Confucius's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yiyou—the first day of the month—the emperor went to Qufu and visited the shrine of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 既尊，將拜。

translations.literal: After the rites of respect were performed, he was about to bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites of respect were complete, he prepared to bow.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「孔子，陪臣也，不當以天子拜之。

translations.literal: Those beside him said: "Confucius was a subject of lower rank—it is not fitting for the Son of Heaven to bow to him."
translations.idiomatic: Those around him said, "Confucius was only a subject. The Son of Heaven should not bow to him."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「孔子百世帝王之師，敢不敬乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Confucius was teacher to emperors for a hundred generations—how would I dare not revere him!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Confucius has been teacher to emperors for a hundred generations. How could I fail to show him reverence?"

sentences.zh: 」遂拜之。

translations.literal: He thereupon bowed.
