translations.idiomatic: He bowed.

sentences.zh: 又拜孔子墓，命葺孔子祠，禁孔林樵采。

translations.literal: He also bowed at Confucius's tomb, ordered Confucius's shrine repaired, and forbade cutting firewood in the Confucian grove.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed at Confucius's tomb as well, ordered the shrine restored, and forbade firewood gathering in the Confucian grove.

sentences.zh: 訪孔子、顏淵之後，以為曲阜令及主簿。

translations.literal: He sought out descendants of Confucius and Yan Yuan and appointed them prefect and chief clerk of Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: He found descendants of Confucius and Yan Yuan and made them prefect and chief clerk of Qufu.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，帝發兗州。

translations.literal: On bingxu the emperor departed from Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the emperor left Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，吳越順德太夫人吳氏卒。

translations.literal: On yiwei Shun'ede Grand Madame Lady Wu of Wuyue died.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Shun'ede Grand Madame Lady Wu of Wuyue died.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，蜀大水入成都，漂沒千餘家，溺死五千餘人，壞太廟四室。

translations.literal: On dingyou great floods entered Chengdu in Shu, drowning more than a thousand households, drowning more than five thousand people, and destroying four chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou a great flood poured into Chengdu in Later Shu, sweeping away more than a thousand households, drowning more than five thousand people, and wrecking four halls of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，蜀大赦，賑水災之家。

translations.literal: On wuxu Shu proclaimed a general amnesty and gave relief to households afflicted by the flood.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Later Shu declared a general amnesty and relief for flood victims.

sentences.zh: 己亥，帝至大梁。

translations.literal: On jihai the emperor reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the emperor returned to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使兼中書令陳留王馮暉卒，其子牙內都虞候繼業殺其兄繼勳，自知軍府事。

translations.literal: Shuofang military commissioner and concurrent Zhongshu Ling Prince of Chenliu Feng Hui died. His son, inner garrison deputy commander Jiye, killed his elder brother Jixun and himself assumed control of the military prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui, Shuofang military commissioner, concurrent Zhongshu Ling, and Prince of Chenliu, died. His son Jiye, deputy commander of the inner garrison, killed his elder brother Jixun and seized control of the command.

sentences.zh: 太子賓客李濤之弟澣，在契丹為勤政殿學士，與幽州節度使蕭海真善。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Guest Li Tao's younger brother Huan, in Khitan service as academician of the Diligent Governance Hall, was on good terms with You Prefecture military commissioner Xiao Haizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, younger brother of Heir Apparent Guest Li Tao, served the Khitan as an academician of the Diligent Governance Hall and was on close terms with Youzhou military commissioner Xiao Haizhen.

sentences.zh: 海真，契丹主兀欲之妻弟也。

translations.literal: Haizhen was the younger brother-in-law of the Khitan ruler Yuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Haizhen was the brother-in-law of the Khitan ruler Yelü Yuzhi.

sentences.zh: 澣說海真內附，海真欣然許之。

translations.literal: Huan persuaded Haizhen to submit inward to the court; Haizhen gladly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan urged Xiao Haizhen to defect to the Chinese court, and Haizhen agreed eagerly.

sentences.zh: 澣因定州諜者田重霸繼絹表以聞，且與濤書，言：「契丹主童騃，專事宴游，無遠志，非前人之比，朝廷若能用兵，必克；

translations.literal: Huan had the Dingzhou spy Tian Chongba carry a memorial written on silk to report it, and also wrote to Tao, saying: "The Khitan ruler is childish and dull, devoting himself only to feasting and pleasure, with no far-reaching ambition—not comparable to his predecessors. If the court can use troops, it will surely conquer;
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan sent the Dingzhou spy Tian Chongba with a silk memorial to report the plot, and wrote to Li Tao as well: "The Khitan ruler is foolish and idle, devoted only to feasting and sport, with no long view—not a man to compare with his predecessors. If the court sends an army, it will surely win;

sentences.zh: 不然，與和，必得。

translations.literal: if not, make peace—and you will surely obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: if not, negotiate peace—and you will surely get it.

sentences.zh: 二者皆利於速，度其情勢，他日終不能力助河東者也。

translations.literal: Both courses profit from speed. Judging their situation and disposition, in days to come they ultimately cannot vigorously aid Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Either course demands haste. Given their temper and circumstances, they will never be able to give Hedong real support in the long run.

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，重霸至大梁，會中國多事，不果從。

translations.literal: On renyin Chongba reached Daliang, but the Central Realm had many affairs underway and the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Tian Chongba reached Daliang, but the court was overwhelmed with other business and never acted on the proposal.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以馮繼業為朔方留後。

translations.literal: On xinhai Feng Jiye was made acting military governor of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Feng Jiye was appointed acting military governor of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王峻，性輕躁，多計數，好權利，喜人附己，自以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Commissioner Wang Jun was by nature rash and impetuous, full of schemes, fond of power and profit, delighted when others attached themselves to him, and regarded himself as bearing the realm on his shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Commissioner Wang Jun was rash and scheming, hungry for power and profit, delighted when men rallied to him, and convinced the fate of the realm rested on his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 每言事，帝從之則喜，或時未允，輒慍懟，往往發不遜語。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke on affairs, if the emperor agreed he rejoiced; if at times he was not granted approval, he would grow angry and resentful and often utter disrespectful words.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he offered counsel, approval made him jubilant; denial sent him into sullen rage, and he often spoke with open disrespect.

sentences.zh: 帝以其故舊，且有佐命功，又素知其為人，每優容之。

translations.literal: Because he was an old associate and had merit in establishing the dynasty, and because the emperor had long known his character, he was always treated with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei indulged him anyway—an old comrade with founding merit, and a man whose faults the emperor had known for years.

sentences.zh: 峻年長於帝，帝即位，猶以兄呼之，或稱其字，峻以是益驕。

translations.literal: Jun was older than the emperor. When the emperor took the throne he still addressed him as elder brother, or sometimes called him by his style name—and Jun grew all the prouder for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was older than the emperor. Even after the enthronement Guo Wei still called him elder brother, or sometimes used his style name—and Jun grew ever more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 副使鄭仁誨、皇城使向訓、恩州團練使李重進，皆帝在籓鎮時腹心將佐也，帝即位，稍稍進用。

translations.literal: Deputy commissioner Zheng Renhui, Imperial City commissioner Xiang Xun, and En Prefecture training commissioner Li Chongjin were all trusted generals and aides from when the emperor was at his princely fief; after he took the throne they were gradually promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioner Zheng Renhui, Imperial City commissioner Xiang Xun, and Enzhou training commissioner Li Chongjin had all been trusted aides when Guo Wei held his princely domain; after his enthronement they were steadily promoted.

sentences.zh: 峻心嫉之，累表稱疾，求解機務，以詗帝意。

translations.literal: Jun envied them in his heart, repeatedly submitted memorials claiming illness and requesting release from confidential duties, to probe the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun resented them and repeatedly memorialized illness, asking to be relieved of confidential duties, to test the emperor's reaction.

sentences.zh: 帝屢遣左右敦諭，峻對使者辭氣亢厲。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent close attendants with earnest exhortations; Jun answered the envoys with overbearing tone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent close attendants again and again to urge him back; Wang Jun answered them with defiant arrogance.

sentences.zh: 又遺諸道節度使書求保證，諸道各獻其書，帝驚駭久之，復遣左右慰勉，令視事，且曰：「卿倘不來，朕且自往。

translations.literal: He also sent letters to the military commissioners of the various circuits seeking guarantees. Each circuit presented its letter; the emperor was alarmed for a long time, then again sent close attendants to comfort and encourage him, ordering him to resume duties, and said: "If you will not come, I shall go to you myself."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote every circuit military commissioner asking them to guarantee his position. When those letters reached court the emperor was shaken for a long while, then sent attendants again to coax him back to work, saying, "If you refuse to come, I will come to you myself."

sentences.zh: 」猶不至。

translations.literal: Still he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He still refused to appear.

sentences.zh: 帝知樞密直學士陳觀與峻親善，令往諭指，觀曰：「陛下但聲言臨幸其第，嚴駕以待之，峻必不敢不來。

translations.literal: The emperor knew that Palace Secretariat Direct Academician Chen Guan was on intimate terms with Jun and sent him to convey the imperial intent. Guan said: "Your Majesty need only announce that you will visit his residence in person and prepare a full imperial escort to await him—Jun will surely not dare fail to come."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Palace Secretariat Direct Academician Chen Guan was close to Wang Jun, the emperor sent him with the message. Chen Guan said, "Your Majesty need only announce a personal visit to his house and muster a full imperial escort to wait there—Wang Jun will not dare stay away."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊子，峻入朝，帝慰勞令視事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuzi, Jun entered court; the emperor comforted and encouraged him and ordered him to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on wuzi, Wang Jun came to court. The emperor soothed him and ordered him back to work.

sentences.zh: 重進，滄州人，其母即帝妹福慶長公主也。

translations.literal: Chongjin was a man of Cang Prefecture; his mother was the emperor's sister, Princess Fuqing the Long.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin was a native of Cangzhou; his mother was the emperor's sister, Princess Fuqing the Long.

sentences.zh: 李穀足跌，傷右臂，在告月餘。

translations.literal: Li Gu stumbled and injured his right arm; he remained on sick leave for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu tripped and injured his right arm, and stayed on sick leave for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 帝以穀職業繁劇，趣令入朝，辭以未任趨拜。

translations.literal: Because Gu's duties were heavy and complex, the emperor urgently ordered him to enter court; he declined on the ground that he was not yet fit for bowing in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His duties were crushing, and the emperor pressed him to return to court. Li Gu pleaded that he was not yet fit to bow in attendance.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔免朝參，但令視事。

translations.literal: On guisi an edict exempted him from court attendance but ordered him to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi an edict excused him from court attendance but required him to keep handling business.

sentences.zh: 蜀工部尚書、判武德軍邵延鈞不禮於監押王承丕，承丕謀作亂。

translations.literal: Shu's Minister of Works and overseer of the Wude army Shao Yanjun showed no courtesy to supervisory commissioner Wang Chengpi; Chengpi plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Shu, Minister of Works and Wude army overseer Shao Yanjun treated supervisory commissioner Wang Chengpi with contempt, and Chengpi plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，左奉聖都指揮使安次孫欽當以部兵戍邊，往辭承丕，承丕邀與俱見府公。

translations.literal: On xinchou Left Fengsheng commander Sun Qin of Anci was to lead his unit to garrison the frontier; he went to take leave of Chengpi, and Chengpi invited him to go together and see the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Sun Qin of Anci, commander of the Left Fengsheng Guard, was due to lead his troops to frontier garrison duty. He came to bid Wang Chengpi farewell, and Chengpi invited him along to call on the prefect.

sentences.zh: 欽不知其謀，從之。

translations.literal: Qin did not know his plot and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qin knew nothing of the plot and went with him.

sentences.zh: 承丕至，則令左右擊殺延鈞，屠其家，稱奉詔處置軍府，即開府庫賞士卒，出系囚，發屯戍。

translations.literal: When Chengpi arrived, he had his attendants strike and kill Yanjun, slaughtered his household, declared that he was acting on imperial orders to take charge of the military prefecture, immediately opened the treasury to reward the soldiers, released prisoners, and mobilized garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, Wang Chengpi had his men kill Shao Yanjun and slaughter his household, claimed he was acting on imperial orders to seize the command, opened the treasury to pay the troops, freed prisoners, and called up the garrisons.

sentences.zh: 將吏畢集，欽謂承丕曰：「今延鈞已伏辜，公宜出詔書以示眾。

translations.literal: When the officers and officials had all assembled, Qin said to Chengpi: "Now that Yanjun has paid for his crime, you ought to produce the imperial edict and show it to the assembly."
translations.idiomatic: When the officers had gathered, Sun Qin told Wang Chengpi, "Yanjun is dead. You should produce the imperial edict and show it to everyone."

sentences.zh: 」承丕曰：「我能致公富貴，勿問詔書。

translations.literal: Chengpi said: "I can make you rich and noble—do not ask about an edict."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengpi said, "I can make you rich—never mind the edict."

sentences.zh: 」欽始知承丕反，因紿曰：「今內外未安，我請以部兵為公巡察。

translations.literal: Qin then knew Chengpi had rebelled and therefore deceived him, saying: "Inside and outside are not yet secure—I ask to lead my unit on patrol for you."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qin then knew Wang Chengpi had rebelled. He lied smoothly: "The city is still unsettled. Let me take my troops out on patrol for you."

sentences.zh: 」即躍馬而出，承丕連呼之，不止。

translations.literal: He immediately leapt on his horse and went out; Chengpi called after him repeatedly, but he would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: He vaulted onto his horse and rode out. Wang Chengpi shouted after him again and again, but he would not turn back.

sentences.zh: 欽至營，曉諭其眾，帥以入府，攻承丕，承丕左右欲拒戰，欽叱之，皆棄兵走，遂執承丕，斬之，並其親黨，傳首成都。

translations.literal: Qin reached the camp, explained the situation at dawn to his men, led them into the prefectural headquarters to attack Chengpi. Chengpi's attendants wished to resist; Qin shouted them down and they all cast aside their weapons and fled. He then seized Chengpi, beheaded him, executed his close associates as well, and sent the head to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qin reached camp, roused his men at dawn, and led them back into headquarters to attack Wang Chengpi. Chengpi's guards tried to fight; Sun Qin roared them down until they dropped their weapons and ran. He seized Chengpi, beheaded him and his partisans, and sent the head to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 天平節度使、守中書令高行周卒。

translations.literal: Tianping military commissioner and acting Zhongshu Ling Gao Xingzhou died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou, Tianping military commissioner and acting Zhongshu Ling, died.

sentences.zh: 行周有勇而知義，功高而不矜，策馬臨敵，叱吒風生，平居與賓僚宴集，侃侃和易，人以是重之。

translations.literal: Xingzhou had courage and understood righteousness; his achievements were high yet he was not arrogant. Galloping to face the enemy, his shouts raised a wind; in ordinary times at banquets with guests and aides he was easy and affable—and on this account people respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou was brave and principled, accomplished yet unassuming. Charging the enemy he thundered; at ease among guests and staff he was warm and easy—and men respected him for both.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，蜀主遣客省使趙季札如梓州，慰撫吏民。

translations.literal: On guimao the Shu ruler dispatched Guest Reception Commissioner Zhao Jizu to Ziz Prefecture to comfort officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Later Shu emperor sent Guest Reception Commissioner Zhao Jizu to Zizhou to reassure officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 漢法，犯私鹽、麴，無問多少抵死。

translations.literal: Under Zhou law, violation of private salt or yeast, regardless of amount, was punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou law, anyone caught with private salt or yeast faced death, no matter how little.

sentences.zh: 鄭州民有以屋稅受鹽於官，過州城，吏以為私鹽，執而殺之，其妻訟冤。

translations.literal: A man of Zheng Prefecture received salt from the government as payment for a house tax, passed through the prefectural city, and the officials took it for private salt, seized him, and killed him. His wife petitioned that he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: A man in Zhengzhou had taken salt from the government in lieu of a house tax. Passing through the prefectural city, officials seized him as a smuggler and executed him. His wife petitioned for justice.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，始詔犯鹽、麴者以斤兩定刑有差。

translations.literal: On guichou an edict was first issued that offenders in salt and yeast would be sentenced according to weight in jin and liang, with differentiated penalties.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the court at last decreed graded punishments for salt and yeast offenses, measured by weight.
